|» tileId|body|string \| null|false|Tile ID for tile-based alerts. Must be a line, stacked bar, or number type tile.|
|» savedSearchId|body|string \| null|false|Saved search ID for saved_search alerts.|
|» groupBy|body|string \| null|false|Group-by key for saved search alerts.|
|» chartConfig|body|[ClickStackAlertChartConfig](#schemaclickstackalertchartconfig)|false|none|
|» threshold|body|number|true|Threshold value for triggering the alert. For between and not_between threshold types, this is the lower bound.|
|» thresholdMax|body|number \| null|false|Upper bound for between and not_between threshold types. Required when thresholdType is between or not_between, must be >= threshold.|
|» interval|body|string|true|Evaluation interval for the alert. `30s` requires the 30s alert interval feature to be enabled for your team. Anomaly alerts (detectionMode "anomaly") support only `5m`, `15m`, `30m`, and `1h`; other intervals are rejected with 400.|
|» scheduleOffsetMinutes|body|integer \| null|false|Offset from the interval boundary in minutes. For example, 2 with a 5m interval evaluates windows at :02, :07, :12, etc. (UTC).|
|» scheduleStartAt|body|string \| null(date-time)|false|Absolute UTC start time anchor. Alert windows start from this timestamp and repeat every interval.|
|» source|body|string|false|Alert source type (tile-based or saved search).|
|» thresholdType|body|string|true|Threshold comparison direction.|
|» channel|body|[ClickStackAlertChannel](#schemaclickstackalertchannel)|false|none|
|» channels|body|[ClickStackAlertChannels](#schemaclickstackalertchannels)|false|Notification channels to trigger when the alert fires or resolves. Between 1 and 10 channels; duplicates are rejected.|
|» name|body|string \| null|false|Alert name template (Handlebars), rendered as the notification title. When omitted, a default title is generated from the display name, value and threshold.|
|» displayName|body|string \| null|false|Display name shown in the alerts list and in notification titles. Defaults to the name of the referenced saved search, dashboard tile, or inline chart when omitted or null.|
|» tags|body|[string]|false|Tags for the alert. Defaults to the tags of the referenced saved search or dashboard when omitted or null; inline alerts have no parent to inherit from and default to an empty list.|
|» message|body|string \| null|false|Alert message template.|
|» note|body|string \| null|false|Freeform note for the alert. Supports markdown formatting.|
|» numConsecutiveWindows|body|integer \| null|false|Fire the alert only after its condition has been met for this many consecutive evaluation windows. While the condition is met but fewer than this many consecutive windows have violated, the alert is in the PENDING state.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» interval|30s|
|» interval|1m|
|» interval|5m|
|» interval|15m|
|» interval|30m|
|» interval|1h|
|» interval|6h|
|» interval|12h|
|» interval|1d|
|» source|saved_search|
|» source|tile|
|» source|inline|
|» thresholdType|above|
|» thresholdType|below|
|» thresholdType|above_exclusive|
|» thresholdType|below_or_equal|
|» thresholdType|equal|
|» thresholdType|not_equal|
|» thresholdType|between|
|» thresholdType|not_between|

`POST /v1/organizations/{organizationId}/services/{serviceId}/clickstack/sources`

**This endpoint is in beta.** API contract is stable, and no breaking changes are expected in the future. <br /><br /> ClickStack: Creates a new source.  The request body is a source object without the `id` field. If an `id` is sent anyway it is silently ignored (stripped before validation — the request is never rejected because of it). Granularity fields (`materializedViews[].minGranularity` and `metadataMaterializedViews.granularity`) accept the same short format the API returns (e.g. `5m`, `15s`, `1h`, `1d`).

`PUT /v1/organizations/{organizationId}/services/{serviceId}/clickstack/sources/{clickStackSourceId}`

**This endpoint is in beta.** API contract is stable, and no breaking changes are expected in the future. <br /><br /> ClickStack: Updates an existing source. The full source object must be provided; this is a replace, not a patch.  The request body is a source object without the `id` field. If an `id` is sent anyway it is silently ignored (stripped before validation — never a 400); the path parameter alone identifies the source. Granularity fields (`materializedViews[].minGranularity` and `metadataMaterializedViews.granularity`) accept the same short format the API returns (e.g. `5m`, `15s`, `1h`, `1d`).

<h3 id="clickstack-update-alert-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organizationId|path|string(uuid)|true|ID of the organization that owns the service.|
|serviceId|path|string(uuid)|true|ID of the ClickStack service.|
|clickStackAlertId|path|string|true|ClickStack Alert ID|
|body|body|[ClickStackUpdateAlertRequest](#schemaclickstackupdatealertrequest)|false|none|
|» dashboardId|body|string \| null|false|Dashboard ID for tile-based alerts.|
|» tileId|body|string \| null|false|Tile ID for tile-based alerts. Must be a line, stacked bar, or number type tile.|
|» savedSearchId|body|string \| null|false|Saved search ID for saved_search alerts.|
|» groupBy|body|string \| null|false|Group-by key for saved search alerts.|
|» chartConfig|body|[ClickStackAlertChartConfig](#schemaclickstackalertchartconfig)|false|none|
|» threshold|body|number|true|Threshold value for triggering the alert. For between and not_between threshold types, this is the lower bound.|
|» thresholdMax|body|number \| null|false|Upper bound for between and not_between threshold types. Required when thresholdType is between or not_between, must be >= threshold.|
|» interval|body|string|true|Evaluation interval for the alert. `30s` requires the 30s alert interval feature to be enabled for your team. Anomaly alerts (detectionMode "anomaly") support only `5m`, `15m`, `30m`, and `1h`; other intervals are rejected with 400.|
|» scheduleOffsetMinutes|body|integer \| null|false|Offset from the interval boundary in minutes. For example, 2 with a 5m interval evaluates windows at :02, :07, :12, etc. (UTC).|
|» scheduleStartAt|body|string \| null(date-time)|false|Absolute UTC start time anchor. Alert windows start from this timestamp and repeat every interval.|
|» source|body|string|false|Alert source type (tile-based or saved search).|
|» thresholdType|body|string|true|Threshold comparison direction.|
|» channel|body|[ClickStackAlertChannel](#schemaclickstackalertchannel)|false|none|
|» channels|body|[ClickStackAlertChannels](#schemaclickstackalertchannels)|false|Notification channels to trigger when the alert fires or resolves. Between 1 and 10 channels; duplicates are rejected.|
|» name|body|string \| null|false|Alert name template (Handlebars), rendered as the notification title. When omitted, a default title is generated from the display name, value and threshold.|
|» displayName|body|string \| null|false|Display name shown in the alerts list and in notification titles. Defaults to the name of the referenced saved search, dashboard tile, or inline chart when omitted or null.|
|» tags|body|[string]|false|Tags for the alert. Defaults to the tags of the referenced saved search or dashboard when omitted or null; inline alerts have no parent to inherit from and default to an empty list.|
|» message|body|string \| null|false|Alert message template.|
|» note|body|string \| null|false|Freeform note for the alert. Supports markdown formatting.|
|» numConsecutiveWindows|body|integer \| null|false|Fire the alert only after its condition has been met for this many consecutive evaluation windows. While the condition is met but fewer than this many consecutive windows have violated, the alert is in the PENDING state.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» interval|30s|
|» interval|1m|
|» interval|5m|
|» interval|15m|
|» interval|30m|
|» interval|1h|
|» interval|6h|
|» interval|12h|
|» interval|1d|
|» source|saved_search|
|» source|tile|
|» source|inline|
|» thresholdType|above|
|» thresholdType|below|
|» thresholdType|above_exclusive|
|» thresholdType|below_or_equal|
|» thresholdType|equal|
|» thresholdType|not_equal|
|» thresholdType|between|
|» thresholdType|not_between|

`PUT /v1/organizations/{organizationId}/services/{serviceId}/clickstack/webhooks/{clickStackWebhookId}`

**This endpoint is in beta.** API contract is stable, and no breaking changes are expected in the future. <br /><br /> ClickStack: Replaces an existing webhook. Readable optional fields (`description`, `body`) are a full replace: omitting them clears them. The write-only fields `headers` and `queryParams` are never returned on read, so omitting them preserves the stored values; send an explicit empty object (`{}`) to clear them. Exception: if the destination (`url` or `service`) changes, omitted `headers`/ `queryParams` are cleared rather than preserved so stored secrets are never forwarded to a new destination.

`DELETE /v1/organizations/{organizationId}/services/{serviceId}/clickstack/webhooks/{clickStackWebhookId}`

**This endpoint is in beta.** API contract is stable, and no breaking changes are expected in the future. <br /><br /> ClickStack: Deletes a webhook.     "whereLanguage": "lucene",
```json
    "orderBy": "Timestamp DESC",
    "tags": [

    ],
```

`PUT /v1/organizations/{organizationId}/services/{serviceId}/clickstack/saved-searches/{clickStackSavedSearchId}`

**This endpoint is in beta.** API contract is stable, and no breaking changes are expected in the future. <br /><br /> ClickStack: Updates an existing saved search. This is a full replace: send the full object. Every optional field (`select`, `where`, `whereLanguage`, `orderBy`, `tags`, `filters`) is always written and falls back to its default when omitted, so omitting a field resets it rather than preserving the stored value.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "Production Errors",
  "sourceId": "507f1f77bcf86cd799439012",
  "select": "Timestamp, ServiceName, Body",
  "where": "SeverityText:ERROR",
  "whereLanguage": "lucene",
  "orderBy": "Timestamp DESC",
  "tags": [
    "production",
    "errors"
  ],
  "filters": [
    "{\"type\":\"sql\",\"condition\":\"ServiceName IN ('checkout', 'payments')\"}"
  ]
}
```

|body|body|[ClickStackSavedSearchInput](#schemaclickstacksavedsearchinput)|false|none|
|» name|body|string|true|Display name for the saved search.|
|» sourceId|body|string|true|ID of the source to query. Must belong to the team.|
|» select|body|string|false|Comma-separated list of column expressions to display. Empty uses the source default.|
|» where|body|string|false|Row filter expression. The language is controlled by whereLanguage.|
|» whereLanguage|body|string|false|Language used for the where filter.|
|» orderBy|body|string|false|ORDER BY expression. Empty uses the source default.|
|» tags|body|[string]|false|Tags used to organize saved searches.|
|» filters|body|[[ClickStackSavedSearchFilter](#schemaclickstacksavedsearchfilter)]|false|Structured pinned filters applied to the search.|

`POST /v1/organizations/{organizationId}/postgres`

**This endpoint is in beta.** API contract is stable, and no breaking changes are expected in the future. <br /><br /> Creates a new Postgres service in the organization and returns it. The service is started asynchronously.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "string",
  "provider": "aws",
  "region": "string",
  "postgresVersion": "18",
  "size": "c6gd.large",
  "haType": "none",
  "tags": [

    }
  ],

    {

      "source": "203.0.113.0/24",
      "portRange": "5432",
      "description": "string"
    }
  ],
  "pgConfig": {
    "max_connections": 100
  },
  "pgBouncerConfig": {
    "default_pool_size": "16"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-new-postgres-service-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organizationId|path|string(uuid)|true|ID of the organization that will own the service.|
|body|body|[PostgresServicePostRequest](#schemapostgresservicepostrequest)|false|none|
|» name|body|[pgNameProperty](#schemapgnameproperty)|true|Name of the Postgres service. Alphanumerical string with whitespaces up to 50 characters.|
|» provider|body|[pgProvider](#schemapgprovider)|true|The cloud provider for a Postgres service.|
|» region|body|[pgRegion](#schemapgregion)|true|The cloud region for a Postgres service.|
|» postgresVersion|body|[pgVersion](#schemapgversion)|false|none|
|» size|body|[pgSize](#schemapgsize)|true|The VM size for a Postgres service.|
|» haType|body|[pgHaType](#schemapghatype)|false|Type of high availability: “none” for no replication, “async” for asynchronous replication to a single standby, and “sync” for synchronous replication to two standbys.|
|» tags|body|[pgTags](#schemapgtags)|false|Tags associated with the Postgres service. Tag keys starting with “chc_” are reserved for internal use.|
|» ipAccessList|body|[[PostgresIpAccessListEntry](#schemapostgresipaccesslistentry)]|false|IPv4 TCP access rules to apply when creating the service. Omit to allow all IPv4 and IPv6 addresses on Postgres (5432) and PgBouncer (6432). Provide an empty list to block public access. When provided, only these rules are allowed; include separate rules for each required port.|
|» pgConfig|body|[pgConfig](#schemapgconfig)|false|Postgres [runtime configuration](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/runtime-config.html) configuration.|
|» pgBouncerConfig|body|[pgBouncerConfig](#schemapgbouncerconfig)|false|PgBouncer [runtime configuration](https://www.pgbouncer.org/config.html) configuration.|

`PATCH /v1/organizations/{organizationId}/postgres/{postgresId}`

**This endpoint is in beta.** API contract is stable, and no breaking changes are expected in the future. <br /><br /> Update a Postgres service that belongs to the organization. **WARNING:** Changing the name also updates the host name and certificates for the service.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "ipAccessList": {
    "add": [
      {
        "id": "string",
        "source": "203.0.113.0/24",
        "portRange": "5432",
        "description": "string"
      }
    ],
    "remove": [
      {
        "id": "string"
      }
    ]
  },
  "name": "string",
  "size": "c6gd.large",
  "haType": "none",
  "tags": [
    {
      "key": "Environment",
      "value": "staging"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-postgresql-service-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organizationId|path|string(uuid)|true|ID of the organization that owns the Postgres service.|
|postgresId|path|string(uuid)|true|ID of the requested Postgres service.|
|body|body|[PostgresServicePatchRequest](#schemapostgresservicepatchrequest)|false|none|
|» ipAccessList|body|[PostgresIpAccessListPatch](#schemapostgresipaccesslistpatch)|false|none|

|» size|body|[pgSize](#schemapgsize)|false|The VM size for a Postgres service.|
|» haType|body|[pgHaType](#schemapghatype)|false|Type of high availability: “none” for no replication, “async” for asynchronous replication to a single standby, and “sync” for synchronous replication to two standbys.|
|» tags|body|[pgTags](#schemapgtags)|false|Tags associated with the Postgres service. Tag keys starting with “chc_” are reserved for internal use.|

<a id="opIdpostgresInstanceMetricsGet"></a>

```bash
curl 'https://api.clickhouse.cloud/v1/organizations/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/postgres/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/metrics?from_date=1970-01-01T00%3A00%3A00Z&to_date=1970-01-01T00%3A00%3A00Z' \
```

`GET /v1/organizations/{organizationId}/postgres/{postgresId}/metrics`

**This endpoint is in beta.** API contract is stable, and no breaking changes are expected in the future. <br /><br /> Returns bucketed time-series metrics for a PostgreSQL service over the requested window (CPU, memory, disk, network, connections, cache hit ratio, throughput, transactions, wait events, lock waits, and more). Use this to chart or analyze how a service behaved over time.

|from_date|query|string(date-time)|true|Inclusive start of the time window (RFC 3339 date-time).|
|to_date|query|string(date-time)|true|Exclusive end of the time window (RFC 3339 date-time).|
|bucket_size_seconds|query|integer|false|Time-series bucket size in seconds. When omitted, a bucket size is derived from the requested window. Requests are capped at 250 data points.|

## List of Postgres service backups

<a id="opIdpostgresServiceBackupGetList"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clickhouse.cloud/v1/organizations/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/postgres/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/backups \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/organizations/{organizationId}/postgres/{postgresId}/backups`

**This endpoint is in beta.** API contract is stable, and no breaking changes are expected in the future. <br /><br /> Returns a list of the base backups retained for a Postgres service, ordered by last modified date, newest first. Results are capped at `limit` (default and maximum 100) per page. Every response carries `limit`, `totalCount` and `nextCursor`; pass `nextCursor` as the `cursor` query parameter to fetch the next page, repeating until it is null. A Postgres service is recovered to a point in time rather than to a single backup, so restore it with the restore endpoint and a timestamp between the service's `earliestRestoreTime` and now, rather than with a backup key from this list.

<h3 id="list-of-postgres-service-backups-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organizationId|path|string(uuid)|true|ID of the organization that owns the Postgres service.|
|postgresId|path|string(uuid)|true|ID of the Postgres service the backups were created from.|
|limit|query|integer|false|Maximum number of results to return.|
|cursor|query|string|false|Opaque cursor from a previous response's `nextCursor`, marking where to resume the list.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "status": 200,
  "requestId": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "result": [
    {
      "key": "basebackups_005/000000010000000000000002_backup_stop_sentinel.json",
      "status": "string",
      "lastModified": "2026-03-31T18:17:37Z"
    }
  ],
  "limit": 0,
  "totalCount": 0,
  "nextCursor": "string"
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "status": 400,
  "error": "string",
  "requestId": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "status": 500,
  "error": "string",
  "requestId": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
}
```

Status Code **200**

## List Postgres server logs

<a id="opIdpostgresLogsGetList"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.clickhouse.cloud/v1/organizations/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/postgres/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/logs?from_date=1970-01-01T00%3A00%3A00Z&to_date=1970-01-01T00%3A00%3A00Z' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/organizations/{organizationId}/postgres/{postgresId}/logs`

**This endpoint is in beta.** API contract is stable, and no breaking changes are expected in the future. <br /><br /> Returns PostgreSQL server log entries for a Postgres service within the given time window, most recent first by default (override with `sort_order`). Results are paginated with `limit`/`offset`; advance `offset` until a page returns fewer than `limit` entries to read the full window. The time range must not exceed 30 days, and `to_date` must be after `from_date`.

<h3 id="list-postgres-server-logs-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organizationId|path|string(uuid)|true|ID of the organization that owns the Postgres service.|
|postgresId|path|string(uuid)|true|ID of the requested Postgres service.|
|from_date|query|string(date-time)|true|Inclusive start of the time window (RFC 3339 date-time).|
|to_date|query|string(date-time)|true|Inclusive end of the time window (RFC 3339 date-time).|
|body_contains|query|string|false|Case-sensitive substring the log body must contain.|
|severity|query|string|false|Filter to log entries with this PostgreSQL severity (for example, ERROR, WARNING, LOG).|
|sort_order|query|string|false|Sort order. One of `asc` or `desc`.|
|limit|query|integer|false|Maximum number of results to return.|
|offset|query|integer|false|Number of results to skip before returning.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|sort_order|asc|
|sort_order|desc|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "status": 200,
  "requestId": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "result": [
    {
      "timestamp": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "severity": "string",
      "body": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "status": 400,
  "error": "string",
  "requestId": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
}
```

```json
}
```

## Attach UDF to service

<a id="opIdudfAttach"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clickhouse.cloud/v1/organizations/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/udfs/string/attachments/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "version": 1
  }'
```

`PUT /v1/organizations/{organizationId}/udfs/{functionName}/attachments/{serviceId}`

Attaches one UDF version to a service, replacing the current version when necessary. When version is omitted, the latest ready version is attached.

```json
{
  "version": 1
}
```

|organizationId|path|string(uuid)|true|ID of the requested organization.|
|functionName|path|string|true|Name of the UDF.|
|serviceId|path|string(uuid)|true|ID of the requested service.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» version|body|integer|false|Version to attach. When omitted, the latest ready version is attached.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
  "status": 200,
  "requestId": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",

    "functionName": "string",
```

## Delete a saved query

<a id="opIdsavedQueryDelete"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clickhouse.cloud/v1/organizations/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/services/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/saved-queries/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`DELETE /v1/organizations/{organizationId}/services/{serviceId}/saved-queries/{queryId}`

Deletes a saved query.

<h3 id="delete-a-saved-query-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organizationId|path|string(uuid)|true|ID of the requested organization.|
|serviceId|path|string(uuid)|true|ID of the requested service.|
|queryId|path|string(uuid)|true|ID of the requested saved query.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "status": 200,
  "requestId": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
  "error": "string",
  "issues": [
    {
      "path": [
        "string"
      ],
      "code": "string",
      "message": "string"
    }
  ],
  "status": 400,
  "requestId": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
  "error": "string",

}
```

```json
  "error": "string",

  "requestId": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
}
```

> 409 Response

```json
  "error": "string",

  "requestId": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
  "error": "string",
```

<h3 id="delete-a-saved-query-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|The saved query was deleted.|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|The request cannot be processed due to a client error. Please verify your request parameters and try again.|Inline|
|403|Forbidden|The request is forbidden.|Inline|
|404|Not Found|Saved query not found.|Inline|
|409|Conflict|Saved query can not be managed via this API.|Inline|
|500|Internal Server Error|An internal server error has occurred. If this issue persists, please contact ClickHouse Cloud support for assistance.|Inline|

<h2 id="tocS_ScalingScheduleEntry">ScalingScheduleEntry</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemascalingscheduleentry"></a>
<a id="schema_ScalingScheduleEntry"></a>
<a id="tocSscalingscheduleentry"></a>
<a id="tocsscalingscheduleentry"></a>

```json
{
  "id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "name": "string",
  "weekdays": [
    0
  ],
  "startHourUtc": 0,
  "endHourUtc": 1,
  "autoscalingMode": "vertical",
  "minReplicaMemoryGb": 0,
  "maxReplicaMemoryGb": 0,
  "minReplicas": 0,
  "maxReplicas": 0,
  "idleScaling": true,
  "idleTimeoutMinutes": 0,
  "isActiveNow": true
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string(uuid)|true|none|Unique identifier for this schedule entry.|
|name|string|true|none|Human-readable label for this schedule entry.|
|weekdays|[integer]|true|none|Days of the week this entry applies to. 0 = Sunday, 1 = Monday, …, 6 = Saturday.|
|startHourUtc|integer|true|none|UTC hour (0–23) when this entry becomes active (inclusive).|
|endHourUtc|integer|true|none|UTC hour (1–24) when this entry deactivates (exclusive). Must differ from startHourUtc. Set to 24 to end at midnight. Values less than startHourUtc create an overnight window spanning midnight.|
|autoscalingMode|string|true|none|Autoscaling mode for this entry. "vertical" runs a fixed replica count while memory scales; "horizontal" scales the replica count at a fixed per-replica memory. Defaults to "vertical" for entries persisted before the mode was exposed.|
|minReplicaMemoryGb|number|false|none|Minimum memory per replica (Gb) during this window. A range in vertical; in horizontal it equals maxReplicaMemoryGb (memory is fixed while the replica count scales).|
|maxReplicaMemoryGb|number|false|none|Maximum memory per replica (Gb) during this window. A range in vertical; in horizontal it equals minReplicaMemoryGb (memory is fixed while the replica count scales).|
|minReplicas|integer|false|none|Minimum number of replicas during this window. For a horizontal entry the replica count scales between minReplicas and maxReplicas; for a vertical entry minReplicas and maxReplicas are equal and report the fixed replica count (both omitted when the entry stored no count).|
|maxReplicas|integer|false|none|Maximum number of replicas during this window. For a horizontal entry the replica count scales between minReplicas and maxReplicas; for a vertical entry minReplicas and maxReplicas are equal and report the fixed replica count (both omitted when the entry stored no count).|
|idleScaling|boolean|false|none|Whether idle scaling is enabled during this window.|
|idleTimeoutMinutes|integer|false|none|Idle timeout in minutes during this window.|
|isActiveNow|boolean|true|none|Whether this entry is currently active. Scheduled times are indicative — actions are applied on a best-effort basis and may be delayed by a few minutes.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|autoscalingMode|vertical|
|autoscalingMode|horizontal|

<h2 id="tocS_ScalingScheduleEntryRequest">ScalingScheduleEntryRequest</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemascalingscheduleentryrequest"></a>
<a id="schema_ScalingScheduleEntryRequest"></a>

<a id="tocsscalingscheduleentryrequest"></a>

```json
{
  "name": "Business hours",
  "weekdays": [
    1,
    2,
    3,
    4,
    5
  ],
  "startHourUtc": 9,
  "endHourUtc": 17,
  "autoscalingMode": "vertical",
  "minReplicaMemoryGb": 16,
  "maxReplicaMemoryGb": 16,
  "numReplicas": 3,
  "minReplicas": 2,
  "maxReplicas": 3,
  "idleScaling": true,
  "idleTimeoutMinutes": 0
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|string|true|none|Human-readable label for this schedule entry.|
|weekdays|[integer]|true|none|Days of the week this entry applies to. 0 = Sunday, 1 = Monday, …, 6 = Saturday.|
|startHourUtc|integer|true|none|UTC hour (0–23) when this entry becomes active (inclusive).|
|endHourUtc|integer|true|none|UTC hour (1–24) when this entry deactivates (exclusive). Must differ from startHourUtc. Set to 24 to end at midnight. Values less than startHourUtc create an overnight window spanning midnight.|
|autoscalingMode|string|false|none|Autoscaling mode for this entry. "vertical" (the default when omitted) runs a fixed replica count while memory scales between minReplicaMemoryGb and maxReplicaMemoryGb; "horizontal" scales the replica count between minReplicas and maxReplicas at a fixed per-replica memory (minReplicaMemoryGb equal to maxReplicaMemoryGb). Horizontal requires the feature to be enabled for the organization.|
|minReplicaMemoryGb|number|false|none|Minimum memory per replica (Gb). Optional for vertical entries — provide both bounds for a memory range, or omit both to inherit memory from the base scaling config. Required for horizontal (both bounds, equal to maxReplicaMemoryGb — memory is fixed while the replica count scales). The upper bound is tier-dependent (lower for non-paid organizations) and enforced when the entry is applied.|
|maxReplicaMemoryGb|number|false|none|Maximum memory per replica (Gb). Optional for vertical entries — provide both bounds for a memory range, or omit both to inherit memory from the base scaling config. Required for horizontal (both bounds, equal to minReplicaMemoryGb — memory is fixed while the replica count scales). The upper bound is tier-dependent (lower for non-paid organizations) and enforced when the entry is applied.|
|numReplicas|integer|false|none|Fixed replica count for a vertical entry (autoscalingMode "vertical" or omitted). Mutually exclusive with minReplicas/maxReplicas. The per-service replica maximum is variable (tier-dependent, configurable per service) and enforced when the entry is applied, not at request time.|
|minReplicas|integer|false|none|Minimum number of replicas. A minReplicas/maxReplicas band scales the replica count in a horizontal entry (autoscalingMode "horizontal"); when autoscalingMode is omitted or "vertical", an equal band (minReplicas === maxReplicas) is instead an accepted vertical fixed count and needs no horizontal entitlement. Must be provided together with maxReplicas. The per-service replica maximum is variable (tier-dependent, configurable per service) and enforced when the entry is applied, not at request time.|
|maxReplicas|integer|false|none|Maximum number of replicas. A minReplicas/maxReplicas band scales the replica count in a horizontal entry (autoscalingMode "horizontal"); when autoscalingMode is omitted or "vertical", an equal band (minReplicas === maxReplicas) is instead an accepted vertical fixed count and needs no horizontal entitlement. Must be provided together with minReplicas. The per-service replica maximum is variable (tier-dependent, configurable per service) and enforced when the entry is applied, not at request time.|
|idleScaling|boolean|false|none|Whether idle scaling is enabled during this window.|
|idleTimeoutMinutes|integer|false|none|Idle timeout in minutes during this window.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|autoscalingMode|vertical|
|autoscalingMode|horizontal|

```json
{
  "effectiveAutoscalingMode": "vertical",

  "effectiveMaxReplicaMemoryGb": 0,

}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|effectiveAutoscalingMode|string|false|none|Autoscaling mode currently in effect on the running service. May diverge from the configured baseline mode while a schedule entry is active.|
|effectiveMinReplicaMemoryGb|number|false|none|Minimum memory per replica (Gb) currently applied to the running service. May diverge from the top-level `minReplicaMemoryGb` baseline while a schedule entry is active.|
|effectiveMaxReplicaMemoryGb|number|false|none|Maximum memory per replica (Gb) currently applied to the running service. May diverge from the top-level `maxReplicaMemoryGb` baseline while a schedule entry is active. Reflects the stored value: normally equal to `effectiveMinReplicaMemoryGb` in horizontal mode, but a legacy service stored with an unequal memory range reports the stored bounds as-is.|
|effectiveMinReplicas|integer|false|none|Minimum number of replicas currently applied to the running service. May diverge from the baseline while a schedule entry is active. Reflects the stored value: normally equal to `effectiveMaxReplicas` in vertical mode (a fixed replica count), but a legacy service stored with an unequal replica range reports the stored bounds as-is.|
|effectiveMaxReplicas|integer|false|none|Maximum number of replicas currently applied to the running service. May diverge from the baseline while a schedule entry is active.|
|effectiveIdleScaling|boolean|false|none|Whether idle scaling is currently in effect on the service. May diverge from the top-level `idleScaling` baseline while a schedule entry is active.|
|effectiveIdleTimeoutMinutes|integer|false|none|Idle timeout in minutes currently in effect on the service. May diverge from the top-level `idleTimeoutMinutes` baseline while a schedule entry is active.|
|activeEntryId|string(uuid)|false|none|ID of the schedule entry whose values are currently applied to the service. Absent when no entry is active.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|effectiveAutoscalingMode|vertical|
|effectiveAutoscalingMode|horizontal|

Minimum memory of three workers during auto-scaling in Gb. Available only for 'production' services. Must be a multiple of 12 and greater than or equal to 24. Always absent for horizontal-autoscaling services (replica count is variable).|
|maxTotalMemoryGb|number|false|none|**Deprecated.** DEPRECATED - inaccurate for services with non-default numbers of replicas. Use `maxReplicaMemoryGb` instead. Maximum memory of three workers during auto-scaling in Gb. Available only for 'production' services. Must be a multiple of 12 and lower than or equal to 360 for non paid services or 1068 for paid services. Always absent for horizontal-autoscaling services (replica count is variable).|
|minReplicaMemoryGb|number|false|none|Minimum total memory of each replica during auto-scaling in Gb. A range in vertical autoscaling; equal to maxReplicaMemoryGb in horizontal (memory is fixed while the replica count scales). Must be a multiple of 4 and greater than or equal to 8.|
|maxReplicaMemoryGb|number|false|none|Maximum total memory of each replica during auto-scaling in Gb. A range in vertical autoscaling; equal to minReplicaMemoryGb in horizontal (memory is fixed while the replica count scales). Must be a multiple of 4 and lower than or equal to 120* for non paid services or 356* for paid services.* - maximum replica size subject to cloud provider hardware availability in your selected region. |
|numReplicas|integer|false|none|Number of replicas for the service. The number of replicas must be between 2 and 50 for the first service in a warehouse. Services that are created in an existing warehouse can have a number of replicas as low as 1. Further restrictions may apply based on your organization's tier and its per-warehouse replica limit. It defaults to 1 for the BASIC tier and 3 for the SCALE and ENTERPRISE tiers. Present only when the service uses vertical autoscaling. For horizontal autoscaling, use minReplicas and maxReplicas instead.|
|minReplicas|integer|false|none|Minimum number of replicas for horizontal autoscaling. Present only when the service uses horizontal autoscaling.|
|maxReplicas|integer|false|none|Maximum number of replicas for horizontal autoscaling. Present only when the service uses horizontal autoscaling.|
|autoscalingMode|string|true|none|Configured autoscaling mode. "vertical" runs a fixed replica count while memory scales between minReplicaMemoryGb and maxReplicaMemoryGb; "horizontal" scales the replica count between minReplicas and maxReplicas at a fixed per-replica memory. This is the baseline configuration; the mode currently applied (which may differ while a schedule entry is active) is currentScaling.effectiveAutoscalingMode.|
|replicaMemoryGb|number|false|none|Fixed memory per replica in Gb for horizontal autoscaling. Present only when the service uses horizontal autoscaling. Must be a multiple of 4, at least 8 Gb, and at most 120 Gb for non paid services or 356 Gb for paid services.|
|idleScaling|boolean|false|none|When set to true the service is allowed to scale down to zero when idle. True by default.|
|idleTimeoutMinutes|number|false|none|Set minimum idling timeout (in minutes). Must be >= 5 minutes.|
|ipAccessList|[[IpAccessListEntry](#schemaipaccesslistentry)]|false|none|List of IP addresses allowed to access the service|
|createdAt|string(date-time)|false|none|Service creation timestamp. ISO-8601.|
|encryptionKey|string|false|none|Optional customer provided disk encryption key|
|encryptionAssumedRoleIdentifier|string|false|none|Optional role to use for disk encryption|
|iamRole|string|false|none|IAM role used for accessing objects in s3|
|privateEndpointIds|[string]|false|none|List of private endpoints|
|availablePrivateEndpointIds|[string]|false|none|List of available private endpoints ids that can be attached to the service|
|dataWarehouseId|string|false|none|Data warehouse containing this service|
|isPrimary|boolean|false|none|True if this service is the primary service in the data warehouse|
|isReadonly|boolean|false|none|True if this service is read-only. It can only be read-only if a dataWarehouseId is provided.|
|releaseChannel|string|false|none|Select fast if you want to get new ClickHouse releases as soon as they are available. You'll get new features faster, but with a higher risk of bugs. Select slow if you would like to defer releases to give yourself more time to test. This feature is only available for production services. default is the regular release channel.|
|byocId|string|false|none|This is the ID returned after setting up a region for Bring Your Own Cloud (BYOC). When the byocId parameter is specified, the minReplicaMemoryGb and the maxReplicaGb parameters are required too, with values included among the following sizes: 48, 116, 172, 232.|
|hasTransparentDataEncryption|boolean|false|none|True if the service should have the Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) enabled. TDE is only available for ENTERPRISE organizations tiers and can only be enabled at service creation.|
|profile|string|false|none|Custom instance profile. Only available for ENTERPRISE and BYOC organization tiers. Standard values: 'v1-default', 'v1-highmem-xs', 'v1-highmem-s', 'v1-highmem-m', 'v1-highmem-l', 'v1-highmem-xl'. BYOC services may instead use a dynamic BYOC profile configured for their infrastructure (e.g. 'v1-standard-byoc-4'); it requires byocId, and minReplicaMemoryGb and maxReplicaMemoryGb must both equal the profile's memory size. Use the serviceProfiles endpoint to list the profiles available to the organization.|
|transparentDataEncryptionKeyId|string|false|none|The ID of the Transparent Data Encryption key used for the service. This is only available if hasTransparentDataEncryption is true.|
|encryptionRoleId|string|false|none|The ID of the IAM role used for encryption. This is only available if hasTransparentDataEncryption is true.|

<h2 id="tocS_BackupEncryptionConfig">BackupEncryptionConfig</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemabackupencryptionconfig"></a>
<a id="schema_BackupEncryptionConfig"></a>
<a id="tocSbackupencryptionconfig"></a>
<a id="tocsbackupencryptionconfig"></a>

```json
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "restore_key_pairs": [
    {
      "customer_managed_encryption_key": {
        "aws_kms_key_arn": "arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111122223333:key/1234abcd-12ab-34cd-56ef-1234567890ab"
      },
      "encrypted_dek": "<base64 wrapped data encryption key>"
    }
  ]
}
```

The `encryption_config.json` stored alongside this backup in your bucket, passed through unchanged. Supply the file contents verbatim rather than constructing this object — its shape is versioned and depends on your cloud provider. See [Export backups to your own cloud account](https://clickhouse.com/docs/cloud/manage/backups/export-backups-to-own-cloud-account) for what it contains.

Accepted only for organizations enrolled in the private preview, and only when the backup is of a service that has transparent data encryption enabled. Such a restore always produces a service with transparent data encryption enabled, inherited from the source service.

<h2 id="tocS_CustomPrivateDnsMapping">CustomPrivateDnsMapping</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacustomprivatednsmapping"></a>
<a id="schema_CustomPrivateDnsMapping"></a>
<a id="tocScustomprivatednsmapping"></a>
<a id="tocscustomprivatednsmapping"></a>

```json
{
  "privateDnsName": "*.my-service.example.com",
  "targetId": "rcfg-097648d8068504966"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|privateDnsName|string|false|none|Optional private DNS names for Reverse Private Endpoint. Can be used as data source destination address. Must be unique across the ClickHouse service.<br>Generally available for Google Private Service Connect (PSC). For AWS PrivateLink (VPC endpoint service and VPC resource), available in Private Preview; contact ClickHouse support to enable it for your service. Not supported for MSK multi-VPC.<br>Supports exact names and leading wildcard names such as *.example.com|
|targetId|string|false|none|Optional DNS target ID. Supported only for VPC_RESOURCE, where it is the CHILD resource configuration ID (rcfg-…), or the configuration ID for a single resource. Set it at create time to route a custom DNS name to that resource. If the target is not reported in dnsTargets yet, the mapping is not served until it appears; it does not fall back to the default target. If omitted, the default target is used. Once dnsTargets is non-empty, adding or changing a targetId requires an ID in that list; unchanged target IDs are not re-checked.|

```json
{
```
```json
  "skipInitialLoad": true,
  "startAfter": "events/2026-06-01/",
  "authentication": "IAM_ROLE",
  "iamRole": "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/MyRole",
  "connectionString": "DefaultEndpointsProtocol=https;AccountName=myaccount;AccountKey=mykey;EndpointSuffix=core.windows.net",
  "path": "data/logs/*.json",
```
```json
  "azureContainerName": "mycontainer",
  "accessKey": {
    "accessKeyId": "string",
    "secretKey": "string"
  },
  "serviceAccountKey": "string"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|skipInitialLoad|boolean \| null|false|none|If set to true, skips the initial load and only ingests files delivered by queue notifications. Only applicable when queueUrl is provided.|
|startAfter|string \| null|false|none|Skip all files up to and including this object key during the initial load. Cannot be provided when skipInitialLoad is true.|
|authentication|string \| null|false|none|Authentication method. IAM_USER is for S3, GCS, and DigitalOcean Spaces. IAM_ROLE is for S3 only. SERVICE_ACCOUNT is for GCS only. For GCS, SERVICE_ACCOUNT_WORKLOAD_IDENTITY is in Private Preview. ClickPipes uses the GCP service account returned in gcpWorkloadIdentity.principal by the operation with operationId clickPipesServiceContextGet; grant it access to the source resources. CONNECTION_STRING is for Azure Blob Storage. PUBLIC uses no authentication.|
|iamRole|string \| null|false|none|IAM role to be used with IAM role authentication. Read more in ClickPipes documentation: https://clickhouse.com/docs/en/integrations/clickpipes/object-storage#authentication|
|connectionString|string \| null|false|none|Connection string for Azure Blob Storage authentication. Required when authentication is CONNECTION_STRING.|
|path|string \| null|false|none|Path to the file(s) within the Azure container. Used for Azure Blob Storage sources. You can specify multiple files using bash-like wildcards. For more information, see the documentation on using wildcards in path: https://clickhouse.com/docs/en/integrations/clickpipes/object-storage#limitations|
|azureContainerName|string \| null|false|none|Container name for Azure Blob Storage. Required when type is azureblobstorage.|
|accessKey|[MskIamUser](#schemamskiamuser) \| null|false|none|none|
|serviceAccountKey|string \| null|false|none|Base64-encoded GCP service account JSON key. Required when authentication is SERVICE_ACCOUNT.|

|Property|Value|

|authentication|IAM_ROLE|
|authentication|IAM_USER|
|authentication|CONNECTION_STRING|
|authentication|SERVICE_ACCOUNT|
|authentication|SERVICE_ACCOUNT_WORKLOAD_IDENTITY|

<h2 id="tocS_ClickPipePostgresPipeSettings">ClickPipePostgresPipeSettings</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaclickpipepostgrespipesettings"></a>
<a id="schema_ClickPipePostgresPipeSettings"></a>
<a id="tocSclickpipepostgrespipesettings"></a>
<a id="tocsclickpipepostgrespipesettings"></a>

```json
{
  "syncIntervalSeconds": 60,
  "pullBatchSize": 1000,
  "publicationName": "clickpipes_publication",
  "replicationMode": "cdc",
  "replicationSlotName": "clickpipes_slot",
  "allowNullableColumns": false,
  "initialLoadParallelism": 1,
  "snapshotNumRowsPerPartition": 100000,
  "snapshotNumberOfParallelTables": 1,
  "enableFailoverSlots": false,
  "deleteOnMerge": false
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|syncIntervalSeconds|integer|false|none|Interval in seconds to sync data from Postgres during CDC replication.|
|pullBatchSize|integer|false|none|Number of rows to pull in each batch during CDC replication.|
|publicationName|string|false|none|PostgreSQL publication name to use for CDC replication. If not provided, ClickPipes will create one automatically.|
|replicationMode|string|false|none|Replication mode: "cdc" (change data capture with initial snapshot), "snapshot" (one-time snapshot only), or "cdc_only" (CDC without initial snapshot).|
|replicationSlotName|string|false|none|PostgreSQL replication slot name. Only valid for "cdc_only" mode. For "cdc" mode, ClickPipes creates the slot automatically.|
|allowNullableColumns|boolean|false|none|Preserve nullability from Postgres in the destination ClickHouse table. When true, columns without NOT NULL constraints are created as Nullable(...). When false, all columns are non-nullable and NULL values are replaced with the default value for the type. Note: Nullable types have performance overhead in ClickHouse.|
|initialLoadParallelism|integer|false|none|Number of parallel workers to use per table in the initial snapshot phase.|
|snapshotNumRowsPerPartition|integer|false|none|Number of rows per partition during the snapshot phase.|
|snapshotNumberOfParallelTables|integer|false|none|Number of tables to snapshot in parallel during the initial load phase.|
|enableFailoverSlots|boolean|false|none|Enable failover support for the replication slot on PG17 and newer. Only applicable when ClickPipes creates the replication slot (i.e., replicationSlotName is NOT provided).|
|deleteOnMerge|boolean|false|none|Enable hard delete behavior in ReplacingMergeTree for PostgreSQL DELETE operations.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|replicationMode|cdc|
|replicationMode|snapshot|
|replicationMode|cdc_only|

<h2 id="tocS_ClickPipePostgresPipeTableMapping">ClickPipePostgresPipeTableMapping</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaclickpipepostgrespipetablemapping"></a>
<a id="schema_ClickPipePostgresPipeTableMapping"></a>
<a id="tocSclickpipepostgrespipetablemapping"></a>
<a id="tocsclickpipepostgrespipetablemapping"></a>

```json
{
  "sourceSchemaName": "public",
  "sourceTable": "users",
  "targetTable": "public_users",
  "excludedColumns": [
    "internal_id",
    "temp_data"
  ],
  "useCustomSortingKey": false,
  "sortingKeys": [
    "created_at_date",
    "event_id"
  ],
  "tableEngine": "ReplacingMergeTree",
  "partitionKey": "id",
  "partitionByExpr": "toYYYYMM(created_at)"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|sourceSchemaName|string|false|none|PostgreSQL source schema name.|
|sourceTable|string|false|none|PostgreSQL source table name.|
|targetTable|string|false|none|ClickHouse target table name, optionally prefixed with schema name (e.g., "my_schema_my_table"). The table will be created automatically if it does not exist. For snapshot mode, the target table must be empty.|
|excludedColumns|[string]|false|none|List of column names to exclude from replication. Column names must be unique within this list.|
|useCustomSortingKey|boolean|false|none|Whether to use a custom sorting key. If true, sortingKeys must be provided. If false or omitted, the default sorting key is the PostgreSQL primary key.|
|sortingKeys|[string]|false|none|Ordered list of column names to use as the sorting (ORDER BY) key in ClickHouse. Only used when useCustomSortingKey is true. Column names must be unique within this list.|
|tableEngine|string|false|none|ClickHouse table engine: "ReplacingMergeTree" (handles updates/deletes), "MergeTree" (append-only), or "Null" (forward data to materialized views without storing it).|
|partitionKey|string|false|none|Custom partitioning column used for parallel snapshotting. Only beneficial for PostgreSQL 13 (no benefit for PG14+, which supports indexed ctid scans). Must be an indexed column of type: `smallint`, `integer`, `bigint`, `timestamp without time zone`, or `timestamp with time zone`. Unrelated to ClickHouse partitioning.|
|partitionByExpr|string|false|none|ClickHouse PARTITION BY expression applied to the destination table when ClickPipes creates it.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|tableEngine|MergeTree|
|tableEngine|ReplacingMergeTree|
|tableEngine|Null|

|targetTable|string|true|none|ClickHouse target table name, optionally prefixed with schema name (e.g., "my_database_my_table"). The table will be created automatically if it does not exist. For snapshot mode, the target table must be empty.|

|useCustomSortingKey|boolean|false|none|Whether to use a custom sorting key. If true, sortingKeys must be provided. If false or omitted, the default sorting key is the MySQL primary key.|
|sortingKeys|[string]|false|none|Ordered list of column names to use as the sorting (ORDER BY) key in ClickHouse. Only used when useCustomSortingKey is true. Column names must be unique within this list.|
|tableEngine|string|false|none|ClickHouse table engine: "ReplacingMergeTree" (handles updates/deletes), "MergeTree" (append-only), or "Null" (forward data to materialized views without storing it).|
|partitionKey|string|false|none|Custom partitioning column used for parallel snapshotting. Must be an indexed column of an integer, date, datetime or timestamp type. Unrelated to ClickHouse partitioning.|
|partitionByExpr|string|false|none|ClickHouse PARTITION BY expression applied to the destination table when ClickPipes creates it.|

```json
{
  "type": "mysql",

  "authentication": "basic",

  "skipCertVerification": false,
  "serverId": 4242,
  "settings": {
    "syncIntervalSeconds": 60,
    "pullBatchSize": 1000,

    "useCompression": false,
    "allowNullableColumns": false,
    "initialLoadParallelism": 1,

      "sourceSchemaName": "my_database",

        "temp_data"

      "useCustomSortingKey": false,
      "sortingKeys": [
        "created_at_date",
        "event_id"
      ],
      "tableEngine": "ReplacingMergeTree",
      "partitionKey": "id",
      "partitionByExpr": "toYYYYMM(created_at)"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h2 id="tocS_ClickPipeBigQueryPipeSettings">ClickPipeBigQueryPipeSettings</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaclickpipebigquerypipesettings"></a>
<a id="schema_ClickPipeBigQueryPipeSettings"></a>
<a id="tocSclickpipebigquerypipesettings"></a>
<a id="tocsclickpipebigquerypipesettings"></a>

```json
{
  "replicationMode": "cdc",
  "replicationMethod": "query_based",
  "syncIntervalSeconds": 60,
  "queryCdcPullSyncParallelism": 4,
  "syncDelaySeconds": 60,
  "pullWindowSizeSeconds": 86400,
  "syncCron": "0 * * * *",
  "allowNullableColumns": true,
  "initialLoadParallelism": 0,
  "snapshotNumRowsPerPartition": 0,
  "snapshotNumberOfParallelTables": 0
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|replicationMode|string|true|none|Replication mode: "cdc" (change data capture with initial snapshot), "snapshot" (one-time snapshot only), or "cdc_only" (CDC without initial snapshot).|
|replicationMethod|string|false|none|How changes are captured from BigQuery. "query_based" polls each table using a watermark timestamp column, "events_based" reads the BigQuery change history using the APPENDS or CHANGES table function. Required for "cdc" and "cdc_only" replication modes and not allowed for "snapshot".|
|syncIntervalSeconds|integer|false|none|Interval in seconds between CDC syncs. Not allowed for "snapshot" replication mode.|
|queryCdcPullSyncParallelism|integer|false|none|Number of tables pulled in parallel during a CDC sync. Not allowed for "snapshot" replication mode.|
|syncDelaySeconds|integer|false|none|Each CDC sync reads data only up to now minus this delay, giving recently written rows time to become visible in BigQuery. Increase it if your tables are loaded via batch jobs or Google Cloud Dataflow; if set too low, late-visible rows may be skipped. Not allowed for "snapshot" replication mode.|
|pullWindowSizeSeconds|integer|false|none|Maximum amount of time one pull (query) can cover. Applies when the pipe has fallen behind, e.g. on the first CDC sync or when resuming after a pause: with a 6 hour limit, a pipe that is 3 days behind catches up in 12 smaller pulls instead of one large query. If a pull fails, only that pull is retried. Not allowed for "snapshot" replication mode.|
|syncCron|string|false|none|Standard 5-field cron expression (or a descriptor such as "@hourly") that schedules CDC syncs, e.g. "0 * * * *" to sync every hour sharp. Evaluated in UTC unless prefixed with "CRON_TZ=<zone>". Must not fire more than once a minute. Syncs run on this schedule instead of every syncIntervalSeconds, so the two cannot both be set. Not allowed for "snapshot" replication mode.|
|allowNullableColumns|boolean|false|none|Allow nullable columns in the destination table.|
|initialLoadParallelism|number|false|none|Number of parallel workers during initial load.|
|snapshotNumRowsPerPartition|number|false|none|Number of rows to snapshot per partition.|
|snapshotNumberOfParallelTables|number|false|none|Number of parallel tables to snapshot.|

```json
    "string"
  ],

  "queryCdcWatermarkColumn": "string",
  "eventsFunction": "appends"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|sourceDatasetName|string|true|none|Source BigQuery dataset name.|
|sourceTable|string|true|none|Source table name.|
|targetTable|string|true|none|Target ClickHouse table name.|
|excludedColumns|[string]|false|none|Columns to exclude from the target table.|
|useCustomSortingKey|boolean|false|none|Whether to use a custom sorting key for the target table.|
|sortingKeys|[string]|false|none|Ordered list of columns to use as sorting key for the target table.|
|tableEngine|string|false|none|Table engine to use for the target table.|
|queryCdcWatermarkColumn|string|false|none|Source column of type TIMESTAMP used as the CDC watermark. Required for every table when replicationMethod is "query_based"; not allowed otherwise.|
|eventsFunction|string|false|none|BigQuery table function used to read changes: "appends" (newly appended rows) or "changes" (all row changes). Required for every table when replicationMethod is "events_based"; not allowed otherwise.|

|---|---|

|tableEngine|ReplacingMergeTree|
|tableEngine|Null|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|syncIntervalSeconds|integer|false|none|Interval in seconds to sync data from MongoDB during CDC replication.|
|pullBatchSize|integer|false|none|Number of rows to pull in each batch during CDC replication.|

|snapshotNumRowsPerPartition|integer|false|none|Number of rows per partition during the snapshot phase.|
|snapshotNumberOfParallelTables|integer|false|none|Number of collections to snapshot in parallel during the initial load phase.|
|deleteOnMerge|boolean|false|none|Enable hard delete behavior in ReplacingMergeTree for MongoDB DELETE operations.|

```json
  "enabled": true,
  "dropUnexpectedValues": false,
  "columns": [

      "name": "amount",
      "type": "Float64"
    }
  ],
  "excludedColumns": [

  ],

    "created_at"
  ],
  "partitionByExpr": "toYYYYMM(created_at)"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|enabled|boolean|true|none|Replicate the collection into typed ClickHouse columns instead of a single JSON document column.|
|dropUnexpectedValues|boolean|false|none|When true, values that don't fit their column are reported with only the field name and reason, without the value.|
|columns|[[ClickPipeMongoDBPipeColumn](#schemaclickpipemongodbpipecolumn)]|false|none|Typed columns of the collection, taken as provided. When omitted, the columns are inferred from a sample of the collection documents. The _id document is always replicated and uses String type.|
|excludedColumns|[string]|false|none|Names of columns, provided or inferred, to leave out of replication. Names that match no column are ignored. Column names must be unique within this list.|
|sortingKeys|[string]|false|none|Ordered list of column names to use as the sorting (ORDER BY) key in ClickHouse. When omitted, the sorting key is the _id document key.|
|partitionByExpr|string|false|none|ClickHouse PARTITION BY expression applied to the destination table when ClickPipes creates it.|

```json
{
  "format": "JSONEachRow",
  "projectId": "my-gcp-project",
  "topic": "my-topic",
  "authentication": "SERVICE_ACCOUNT",
  "seekType": "earliest",
  "seekTimestamp": "2026-04-10T12:00:00Z",
  "filter": "string",
  "enableOrdering": true,
  "ackDeadline": 10
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|format|string|true|none|Format of messages in the Pub/Sub topic. GCP Pub/Sub ClickPipes are in private preview — contact support to enable this feature for your organization.|
|projectId|string|true|none|GCP project ID that owns the Pub/Sub topic.|
|topic|string|true|none|Pub/Sub topic name (not the fully-qualified path).|
|authentication|string|true|none|Authentication method to use with GCP Pub/Sub. SERVICE_ACCOUNT_WORKLOAD_IDENTITY is in Private Preview. ClickPipes uses the GCP service account returned in gcpWorkloadIdentity.principal by the operation with operationId clickPipesServiceContextGet; grant it access to the source resources.|
|seekType|string|true|none|Starting position strategy for consuming the subscription. The seekTimestamp companion is required only when seekType is "timestamp"; setting it for a mismatched seek type is rejected.|
|seekTimestamp|string \| null(date-time)|false|none|RFC 3339 / ISO 8601 timestamp to seek to. Required when seekType is "timestamp"; must be omitted otherwise.|
|filter|string \| null|false|none|Optional Pub/Sub subscription filter expression (CEL). Maximum 256 characters.|
|enableOrdering|boolean \| null|false|none|Whether to enable ordered delivery of messages (requires messages to be published with ordering keys).|
|ackDeadline|integer \| null|false|none|Acknowledgement deadline for messages, in seconds. Must be between 10 and 600.|

#### Enumerated Values

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|object_storage_max_insert_bytes|integer \| null|false|none|Max insert bytes. Number of bytes to process in a single insert batch|
|object_storage_max_file_count|integer \| null|false|none|Max file count. Maximum number of files to process in a single insert batch|
|clickhouse_max_threads|integer \| null|false|none|Max threads. Maximum number of concurrent threads for file processing|
|clickhouse_max_insert_threads|integer \| null|false|none|Max insert threads. Maximum number of concurrent insert threads|
|clickhouse_min_insert_block_size_bytes|integer \| null|false|none|Min insert block size bytes. Minimum size of data block for insert (in bytes)|
|clickhouse_max_download_threads|integer \| null|false|none|Max download threads. Maximum number of concurrent download threads|
|clickhouse_parallel_distributed_insert_select|integer \| null|false|none|Parallel distributed insert select. Only applies when object_storage_use_cluster_function is enabled. When disabled, this setting is ignored and the effective value is 0.|
|kafka_read_committed|boolean|false|none|Kafka Read Committed. Whether Kafka consumers read only committed messages|
|object_storage_use_cluster_function|boolean \| null|false|none|use cluster function. Whether to use ClickHouse cluster function for distributed processing|
|clickhouse_parallel_view_processing|boolean \| null|false|none|parallel view processing. Whether to enable pushing to attached views concurrently instead of sequentially|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string(uuid)|false|none|Unique ClickPipe ID.|
|serviceId|string(uuid)|false|none|ID of the service this ClickPipe belongs to.|
|name|string|false|none|Name of the ClickPipe.|
|state|string|false|none|Current lifecycle state of the ClickPipe. For database pipes: "Provisioning" (initial setup), "Setup" (configuring replication), "Snapshot" (initial data load), "Running" (actively replicating), "Pausing" (transitioning to paused state), "Paused" (temporarily paused), "Modifying" (applying configuration updates), "Resync" (swapping resync tables with original tables), "Failed" (error occurred), "Unknown". For streaming/object storage pipes (Kafka, Kinesis, S3): "Unknown" (initial state), "Provisioning" (setting up resources), "Running" (actively ingesting data), "Stopping" (transitioning to stopped state), "Stopped" (manually stopped, can be restarted), "Completed" (batch ingestion finished for object storage), "Failed" (error occurred, pipe stopped), "InternalError" (internal system error).|
|scaling|[ClickPipeScaling](#schemaclickpipescaling)|false|none|none|
|source|[ClickPipeSource](#schemaclickpipesource)|false|none|none|
|destination|[ClickPipeDestination](#schemaclickpipedestination)|false|none|none|
|fieldMappings|[[ClickPipeFieldMapping](#schemaclickpipefieldmapping)]|false|none|Field mappings of the ClickPipe. Note that all destination columns must be included in the mappings.|
|settings|[ClickPipeSettings](#schemaclickpipesettings)|false|none|none|
|createdAt|string(date-time)|false|none|Creation timestamp of the ClickPipe in ISO 8601 format.|
|updatedAt|string(date-time)|false|none|Last update timestamp of the ClickPipe in ISO 8601 format.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|state|Unknown|
|state|Provisioning|
|state|Running|
|state|Degraded|
|state|Stopping|
|state|Stopped|
|state|Failed|
|state|Completed|
|state|InternalError|
|state|Setup|
|state|Snapshot|
|state|Paused|
|state|Pausing|
|state|Modifying|
|state|Resync|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|streaming_max_insert_wait_ms|integer|false|none|Streaming max insert wait time. Configures the max wait period before inserting data into the ClickHouse.|
|object_storage_concurrency|integer|false|none|Object storage concurrency. Number of concurrent file processing threads|
|object_storage_polling_interval_ms|integer|false|none|Object storage polling interval. Configures the refresh interval for querying continuous ingest for new object storage data|
|object_storage_max_insert_bytes|integer|false|none|Max insert bytes. Number of bytes to process in a single insert batch|
|object_storage_max_file_count|integer|false|none|Max file count. Maximum number of files to process in a single insert batch|
|clickhouse_max_threads|integer|false|none|Max threads. Maximum number of concurrent threads for file processing|
|clickhouse_max_insert_threads|integer|false|none|Max insert threads. Maximum number of concurrent insert threads|
|clickhouse_min_insert_block_size_bytes|integer|false|none|Min insert block size bytes. Minimum size of data block for insert (in bytes)|
|clickhouse_max_download_threads|integer|false|none|Max download threads. Maximum number of concurrent download threads|
|clickhouse_parallel_distributed_insert_select|integer|false|none|Parallel distributed insert select. Only applies when object_storage_use_cluster_function is enabled. When disabled, this setting is ignored and the effective value is 0.|
|kafka_read_committed|boolean|false|none|Kafka Read Committed. Whether Kafka consumers read only committed messages|
|object_storage_use_cluster_function|boolean|false|none|use cluster function. Whether to use ClickHouse cluster function for distributed processing|
|clickhouse_parallel_view_processing|boolean|false|none|parallel view processing. Whether to enable pushing to attached views concurrently instead of sequentially|

```json
{
  "aggFn": "count",
  "valueExpression": "Duration",
  "alias": "Request Duration",
  "level": 0,
  "where": "service:api",
  "whereLanguage": "sql",
  "metricName": "http.server.duration",
  "metricType": "sum",
  "periodAggFn": "delta",
  "numberFormat": {
    "output": "number",
    "mantissa": 2,
    "thousandSeparated": true,
    "average": false,
    "decimalBytes": false,
    "factor": 1,
    "currencySymbol": "$",
    "numericUnit": "bytes_iec",
    "unit": "ms"
  }
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|aggFn|string|true|none|Aggregation function to apply. "count" does not require a valueExpression; "quantile" requires a level field indicating the desired percentile (e.g., 0.95).|
|valueExpression|string|false|none|Expression for the column or value to aggregate. Must be omitted when aggFn is "count"; required for all other aggFn values.|
|alias|string|false|none|Display alias for this select item in chart legends.|
|level|number|false|none|Percentile level; only valid when aggFn is "quantile". Allowed values: 0.5, 0.9, 0.95, 0.99.|
|where|string|false|none|SQL or Lucene filter condition applied before aggregation.|
|whereLanguage|string|false|none|Query language for the where clause.|
|metricName|string|false|none|Name of the metric to aggregate; only applicable when the source is a metrics source.|
|metricType|string|false|none|Metric type; only applicable when the source is a metrics source.|
|periodAggFn|string|false|none|Optional period aggregation function for Gauge metrics (e.g., compute the delta over the period).|
|numberFormat|[ClickStackNumberFormat](#schemaclickstacknumberformat)|false|none|none|

<h2 id="tocS_ClickStackLineBuilderChartConfig">ClickStackLineBuilderChartConfig</h2>

```json
{
  "displayType": "line",
  "sourceId": "65f5e4a3b9e77c001a111111",
  "select": [
    {
      "aggFn": "count",
      "valueExpression": "Duration",
      "alias": "Request Duration",
      "level": 0,
      "where": "service:api",
      "whereLanguage": "sql",
      "metricName": "http.server.duration",
      "metricType": "sum",
      "periodAggFn": "delta",
      "numberFormat": {
        "output": "number",
        "mantissa": 2,
        "thousandSeparated": true,
        "average": false,
        "decimalBytes": false,
        "factor": 1,
        "currencySymbol": "$",
        "numericUnit": "bytes_iec",
        "unit": "ms"
      }
    }
  ],
  "groupBy": "host",
  "asRatio": true,
  "alignDateRangeToGranularity": true,
  "fillNulls": true,
  "fitYAxisToData": true,
  "lineInterpolation": "step",
  "numberFormat": {
    "output": "number",
    "mantissa": 2,
    "thousandSeparated": true,
    "average": false,
    "decimalBytes": false,
    "factor": 1,
    "currencySymbol": "$",
    "numericUnit": "bytes_iec",
    "unit": "ms"
  },
  "compareToPreviousPeriod": true,
  "seriesLimit": 5,
  "formulas": [
    {
      "expression": "A / (A + B) * 100",
      "alias": "Success rate %",
      "numberFormat": {
        "output": "number",
        "mantissa": 2,
        "thousandSeparated": true,
        "average": false,
        "decimalBytes": false,
        "factor": 1,
        "currencySymbol": "$",
        "numericUnit": "bytes_iec",
        "unit": "ms"
      }
    }
  ],
  "showOperandSeries": true
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|displayType|string|true|none|Display type discriminator. Must be "line" for line charts.|
|sourceId|string|true|none|ID of the data source to query.|
|select|[[ClickStackSelectItem](#schemaclickstackselectitem)]|true|none|One or more aggregated values to plot. When asRatio is true, exactly two select items are required.|
|groupBy|string|false|none|Field expression to group results by (creates separate lines per group value).|
|asRatio|boolean|false|none|Plot select[0] / select[1] as a ratio. Requires exactly two select items.|
|alignDateRangeToGranularity|boolean|false|none|Expand date range boundaries to the query granularity interval.|
|fillNulls|boolean|false|none|Fill missing time buckets with zero instead of leaving gaps.|
|fitYAxisToData|boolean|false|none|Set the y-axis lower bound to the minimum of the displayed data instead of zero, making small fluctuations between series easier to see.|
|lineInterpolation|string|false|none|How points are connected. Defaults to "smooth" when omitted.|
|numberFormat|[ClickStackNumberFormat](#schemaclickstacknumberformat)|false|none|none|
|compareToPreviousPeriod|boolean|false|none|Overlay the equivalent previous time period for comparison.|
|seriesLimit|integer|false|none|Maximum number of series rendered (top-N by value). Omit to use the default render cap, set 0 for unlimited, or a positive N to keep the top N series.|
|formulas|[[ClickStackFormula](#schemaclickstackformula)]|false|none|Derived series computed from the select items via letter-ref arithmetic ("A" = select[0], "B" = select[1], ...). Metric, log, and trace sources only. Cannot be combined with asRatio.|
|showOperandSeries|boolean|false|none|Only meaningful with formulas. When false, only the formula series are returned; the raw operand series are hidden.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|displayType|line|
|lineInterpolation|smooth|
|lineInterpolation|linear|
|lineInterpolation|step|

|fillNulls|boolean|false|none|Fill missing time buckets with zero instead of leaving gaps.|
|numberFormat|[ClickStackNumberFormat](#schemaclickstacknumberformat)|false|none|none|

|formulas|[[ClickStackFormula](#schemaclickstackformula)]|false|none|Derived series computed from the select items via letter-ref arithmetic ("A" = select[0], "B" = select[1], ...). Metric, log, and trace sources only. Cannot be combined with asRatio.|
|showOperandSeries|boolean|false|none|Only meaningful with formulas. When false, only the formula series are returned; the raw operand series are hidden.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|displayType|string|true|none|Display type discriminator. Must be "stacked_line" for stacked-line charts.|
|sourceId|string|true|none|ID of the data source to query.|
|select|[[ClickStackSelectItem](#schemaclickstackselectitem)]|true|none|One or more aggregated values to plot. When asRatio is true, exactly two select items are required.|
|groupBy|string|false|none|Field expression to group results by (creates separate stacked bands per group value).|
|asRatio|boolean|false|none|Plot select[0] / select[1] as a ratio. Requires exactly two select items.|
|alignDateRangeToGranularity|boolean|false|none|Align the date range boundaries to the query granularity interval.|
|fillNulls|boolean|false|none|Fill missing time buckets with zero instead of leaving gaps.|
|lineInterpolation|string|false|none|How points are connected. Defaults to "linear" when omitted.|
|numberFormat|[ClickStackNumberFormat](#schemaclickstacknumberformat)|false|none|none|
|seriesLimit|integer|false|none|Maximum number of series rendered (top-N by value). Omit to use the default render cap, set 0 for unlimited, or a positive N to keep the top N series.|
|formulas|[[ClickStackFormula](#schemaclickstackformula)]|false|none|Derived series computed from the select items via letter-ref arithmetic ("A" = select[0], "B" = select[1], ...). Metric, log, and trace sources only. Cannot be combined with asRatio.|
|showOperandSeries|boolean|false|none|Only meaningful with formulas. When false, only the formula series are returned; the raw operand series are hidden.|
|name|string|false|none|Display name for the alert query. Used in notification titles and as an alert-name fallback when the alert itself has no name.|
|where|string|false|none|Chart-level filter applied on top of every select item's own "where" (combined via AND). Builder variants only; rejected on Raw SQL variants (filter inside the sqlTemplate instead).|
|whereLanguage|string|false|none|Language of the chart-level "where" filter.|

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|displayType|stacked_line|
|lineInterpolation|smooth|
|lineInterpolation|linear|
|lineInterpolation|step|
|whereLanguage|sql|
|whereLanguage|lucene|

|scheduleStartAt|string \| null(date-time)|false|none|Absolute UTC start time anchor. Alert windows start from this timestamp and repeat every interval.|

|message|string \| null|false|none|Alert message template.|
|note|string \| null|false|none|Freeform note for the alert. Supports markdown formatting.|
|numConsecutiveWindows|integer \| null|false|none|Fire the alert only after its condition has been met for this many consecutive evaluation windows. While the condition is met but fewer than this many consecutive windows have violated, the alert is in the PENDING state.|
|displayName|string|true|none|The display name for the alert in the UI. Derived from the saved search name, dashboard tile name, or inline chartConfig name when not explicitly set.|
|tags|[string]|true|none|The tags for the alert. Derived from the tags of the referenced saved search or dashboard when not explicitly set; inline alerts default to an empty list.|
|id|string|false|none|Unique alert identifier.|
|state|string|false|none|Current alert state.|
|teamId|string|false|none|Team identifier.|
|silenced|[ClickStackAlertSilenced](#schemaclickstackalertsilenced) \| null|false|none|none|
|executionErrors|[[ClickStackAlertExecutionError](#schemaclickstackalertexecutionerror)]|false|none|Errors recorded during the most recent alert execution, if any.|

<h2 id="tocS_ClickStackTableBuilderChartConfig">ClickStackTableBuilderChartConfig</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaclickstacktablebuilderchartconfig"></a>
<a id="schema_ClickStackTableBuilderChartConfig"></a>
<a id="tocSclickstacktablebuilderchartconfig"></a>
<a id="tocsclickstacktablebuilderchartconfig"></a>

```json
{
  "displayType": "table",
  "sourceId": "65f5e4a3b9e77c001a111111",
  "select": [
    {
      "aggFn": "count",
      "valueExpression": "Duration",
      "alias": "Request Duration",
      "level": 0,
      "where": "service:api",
      "whereLanguage": "sql",
      "metricName": "http.server.duration",
      "metricType": "sum",
      "periodAggFn": "delta",
      "numberFormat": {
        "output": "number",
        "mantissa": 2,
        "thousandSeparated": true,
        "average": false,
        "decimalBytes": false,
        "factor": 1,
        "currencySymbol": "$",
        "numericUnit": "bytes_iec",
        "unit": "ms"
      }
    }
  ],
  "groupBy": "service",
  "having": "count > 100",
  "orderBy": "count DESC",
  "asRatio": false,
  "numberFormat": {
    "output": "number",
    "mantissa": 2,
    "thousandSeparated": true,
    "average": false,
    "decimalBytes": false,
    "factor": 1,
    "currencySymbol": "$",
    "numericUnit": "bytes_iec",
    "unit": "ms"
  },
  "groupByColumnsOnLeft": false,
  "onClick": {
    "type": "search",
    "target": {
      "mode": "id",
      "id": "65f5e4a3b9e77c001a567890"
    },
    "whereTemplate": "ServiceName = '{{ServiceName}}'",
    "whereLanguage": "sql",
    "filters": [
      {
        "kind": "expressionTemplate",
        "expression": "ServiceName",
        "template": "{{ServiceName}}"
      }
    ]
  },
  "formulas": [
    {
      "expression": "A / (A + B) * 100",
      "alias": "Success rate %",
      "numberFormat": {
        "output": "number",
        "mantissa": 2,
        "thousandSeparated": true,
        "average": false,
        "decimalBytes": false,
        "factor": 1,
        "currencySymbol": "$",
        "numericUnit": "bytes_iec",
        "unit": "ms"
      }
    }
  ],
  "showOperandSeries": true
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|displayType|string|true|none|Display type discriminator. Must be "table" for table charts.|
|sourceId|string|true|none|ID of the data source to query.|
|select|[[ClickStackSelectItem](#schemaclickstackselectitem)]|true|none|One or more aggregated values to display as table columns. When asRatio is true, exactly two select items are required.|
|groupBy|string|false|none|Field expression to group results by (one row per group value).|
|having|string|false|none|Post-aggregation SQL HAVING condition.|
|orderBy|string|false|none|SQL ORDER BY expression for sorting table rows.|
|asRatio|boolean|false|none|Display select[0] / select[1] as a ratio. Requires exactly two select items.|
|numberFormat|[ClickStackNumberFormat](#schemaclickstacknumberformat)|false|none|none|
|groupByColumnsOnLeft|boolean|false|none|When true, render Group By columns to the left of series columns in the table. Defaults to false (Group By columns on the right).|
|onClick|[ClickStackOnClick](#schemaclickstackonclick)|false|none|none|
|formulas|[[ClickStackFormula](#schemaclickstackformula)]|false|none|Derived columns computed from the select items via letter-ref arithmetic ("A" = select[0], "B" = select[1], ...). Metric, log, and trace sources only. Cannot be combined with asRatio.|
|showOperandSeries|boolean|false|none|Only meaningful with formulas. When false, only the formula columns are returned; the raw operand columns are hidden.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|displayType|table|

```json
{
  "displayType": "pie",
  "sourceId": "65f5e4a3b9e77c001a111111",
  "select": [
    {
      "aggFn": "count",
      "valueExpression": "Duration",
      "alias": "Request Duration",
      "level": 0,
      "where": "service:api",
      "whereLanguage": "sql",
      "metricName": "http.server.duration",
      "metricType": "sum",
      "periodAggFn": "delta",
      "numberFormat": {
        "output": "number",
        "mantissa": 2,
        "thousandSeparated": true,
        "average": false,
        "decimalBytes": false,
        "factor": 1,
        "currencySymbol": "$",
        "numericUnit": "bytes_iec",
        "unit": "ms"
      }
    }
  ],
  "groupBy": "service",
  "orderBy": "\"Count\" DESC",
  "numberFormat": {
    "output": "number",
    "mantissa": 2,
    "thousandSeparated": true,
    "average": false,
    "decimalBytes": false,
    "factor": 1,
    "currencySymbol": "$",
    "numericUnit": "bytes_iec",
    "unit": "ms"
  },
  "limit": 10
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|displayType|string|true|none|Display type discriminator. Must be "pie" for pie charts.|
