|groupBy|string|false|none|Field expression to group results by (one slice per group value).|
|orderBy|string|false|none|Optional custom SQL ORDER BY expression (raw SQL). Overrides the default value-descending ordering and, when combined with "limit", controls which slices are kept.|
|numberFormat|[ClickStackNumberFormat](#schemaclickstacknumberformat)|false|none|none|
|limit|integer|false|none|Maximum number of slices (SQL LIMIT). Without a custom "orderBy" the query keeps the groups with the largest aggregated values; with an "orderBy" it keeps the first slices in that order. Omit or set 0 to fetch all groups.|

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|displayType|pie|

  ],

  "isVariableEnabled": true,
  "variableName": "environment",
  "minSelections": 1,
  "isGlobalRequirement": true,
  "maxSelections": 1
}

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|true|none|Filter type discriminator. Must be "QUERY_EXPRESSION".|
|name|string|true|none|Display name for the dashboard filter key|
|expression|string|true|none|SQL expression used when querying values for this filter, and when applying this dashboard filter to tiles.|
|sourceId|string|true|none|Source ID this dashboard filter key applies to|
|sourceMetricType|string|false|none|Metric type when source is metrics|
|where|string|false|none|Optional WHERE condition to scope which rows this filter key reads values from|
|whereLanguage|string|false|none|Language of the where condition|
|appliesToSourceIds|[string]|false|none|Optional list of source IDs this filter applies to. Omit or provide an empty array to apply the filter to ALL tiles regardless of source. A non-empty array restricts the filter to only tiles whose source ID is in the list; tiles using other sources are not affected by the selected filter value(s). Scopes the broadcast condition only, so a non-empty array is rejected when isBroadcastEnabled is false, and is omitted from responses for such a filter.|
|isBroadcastEnabled|boolean|false|none|Whether the selected value is applied as a filter condition on every builder tile this filter applies to (see appliesToSourceIds), and every raw sql tile using the $__filters macro. Omitting the field means enabled.|
|isVariableEnabled|boolean|false|none|Whether the selected value is exposed to tile queries as a dashboard variable named by variableName. Tiles may reference it as `$variableName` or using the (preferred) `$__filter($<variableName>)` and `$__conditionalAll(<condition>, $<variableName>)` macros.|
|variableName|string|false|none|Token tiles reference this filter's selected value by, as `$variableName`. Must start with a letter and may contain only letters, numbers, and underscores. Defaults to the display name with whitespace replaced by underscores and remaining illegal characters removed, so a variable-enabled filter whose name derives nothing usable must send this field explicitly. Variable names must be unique across a dashboard's variable-enabled filters. Names the variable only, so the field is rejected when isVariableEnabled is not true, and is omitted from responses for such a filter.|
|minSelections|integer|false|none|Minimum number of values that must be selected before tiles load. Set to 1 to make the filter required. Only 0 and 1 are accepted. Omit the field (or send 0) for the default optional behavior.|
|isGlobalRequirement|boolean|false|none|Widens a required filter's block to every tile on the dashboard. False (the default) blocks only the tiles that read the filter: those referencing its variableName, and those its broadcast applies to. Ignored unless minSelections is 1.|
|maxSelections|integer|false|none|Maximum number of values that can be selected at once. Set to 1 to make the filter single-select. Omit the field for the default multi-select behavior.|

|kind|string|true|none|Source kind discriminator. Must be "log" for log sources.|

|querySettings|[[ClickStackQuerySetting](#schemaclickstackquerysetting)]|false|none|Optional ClickHouse query settings applied when querying this source.|
|filterSettings|[ClickStackSourceFilterSettings](#schemaclickstacksourcefiltersettings) \| null|false|none|none|
|defaultTableSelectExpression|string|true|none|Default columns selected in search results (this can be customized per search later)|

|serviceNameExpression|string \| null|false|none|Expression to extract the service name from log rows.|
|serviceVersionExpression|string \| null|false|none|Expression identifying the running release of a service. Defaults to the OpenTelemetry service.version resource attribute when unset. Where services carry the release on different attributes, fall back across them with coalesce(nullIf(a, ''), nullIf(b, '')).|
|severityTextExpression|string \| null|false|none|Expression to extract the severity/log level text.|
|severityNumberExpression|string \| null|false|none|Expression for the numeric OpenTelemetry SeverityNumber (1-24).|
|bodyExpression|string \| null|false|none|Expression to extract the log message body.|
|eventNameExpression|string \| null|false|none|Expression for the OpenTelemetry log EventName.|
|eventAttributesExpression|string \| null|false|none|Expression to extract event-level attributes.|
|resourceAttributesExpression|string \| null|false|none|Expression to extract resource-level attributes.|
|displayedTimestampValueExpression|string \| null|false|none|This DateTime column is used to display and order search results.|
|orderByExpression|string|false|none|Custom ORDER BY expression that overrides the default ordering. Leave empty to use the auto-detected default.|
|metricSourceId|string \| null|false|none|HyperDX Source for metrics associated with logs. Optional|
|traceSourceId|string \| null|false|none|HyperDX Source for traces associated with logs. Optional|
|traceIdExpression|string \| null|false|none|Expression to extract the trace ID for correlating logs with traces.|
|spanIdExpression|string \| null|false|none|Expression to extract the span ID for correlating logs with traces.|
|implicitColumnExpression|string \| null|false|none|Column used for full text search if no property is specified in a Lucene-based search. Typically the message body of a log.|
|knownColumnsListExpression|string \| null|false|none|For Distributed table sources whose target tables have non-matching column sets. A list of columns supported across all target tables, used instead of SELECT * when fetching full row data. Leave blank to select all columns.|
|useTextIndexForImplicitColumn|string \| null|false|none|Controls whether lucene rendering uses ClickHouse text indices via hasAllTokens() against the implicit column. "auto" detects a covering index at query time, "enabled" forces text index usage, "disabled" forces a LIKE/hasToken fallback.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|string|true|none|Stable identifier of the notification type. Never renamed or reused.|

|severity|string|true|none|Relative importance of notifications of this type.|
|resourceType|string|true|none|Kind of resource a notification of this type is about. Current values: service, organization, clickpipe, postgres. New values may be added over time.|
|isConfigurable|boolean|true|none|Whether the per-role delivery default can be changed. When false the role default is frozen; this does not mean the notification is always delivered.|
|isAvailable|boolean|true|none|False when the caller lacks the permission this type requires. The type is still returned, just flagged.|

<h2 id="tocS_pgConfig">pgConfig</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemapgconfig"></a>
<a id="schema_pgConfig"></a>
<a id="tocSpgconfig"></a>
<a id="tocspgconfig"></a>

```json
{
  "max_connections": 100
}
```

Postgres [runtime configuration](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/runtime-config.html) configuration.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|max_connections|string \| integer|false|none|Sets the maximum number of concurrent connections to the database server.|
|default_transaction_isolation|string|false|none|Sets the default transaction isolation level for new transactions.|
|ssl_min_protocol_version|string|false|none|Sets the minimum SSL/TLS protocol version allowed for client connections.|
|default_toast_compression|string|false|none|Sets the default compression method for compressible values stored out of line (TOAST).|
|maintenance_work_mem|string \| integer|false|none|Sets the maximum memory to be used for maintenance operations.|
|work_mem|string \| integer|false|none|Sets the amount of memory Postgres will use for internal operations like sorting and hashing as part of executing a query.|
|effective_cache_size|string \| integer|false|none|Sets the planner's assumption about the total size of data caches.|
|random_page_cost|string \| number|false|none|Sets the planner's estimate of the cost of a non-sequentially-fetched disk page. Lower values (1.1-1.5) are better for SSDs.|
|effective_io_concurrency|string \| integer|false|none|Number of concurrent disk I/O operations the planner expects. Higher values (100-200) benefit SSDs.|
|max_worker_processes|string \| integer|false|none|Maximum number of background processes the system can support. Includes parallel query workers, logical replication, and more.|
|max_parallel_workers|string \| integer|false|none|Maximum number of workers that can be used for parallel operations. Cannot exceed max_worker_processes.|
|max_parallel_workers_per_gather|string \| integer|false|none|Maximum number of parallel workers per executor node for parallel queries. Use 0 to disable parallel queries.|
|max_parallel_maintenance_workers|string \| integer|false|none|Maximum number of parallel workers for maintenance operations like CREATE INDEX and VACUUM.|
|shared_memory_percent|string \| integer|false|none|Percent of VM memory reserved for the shared_memory, from 25% to 75%. shared_buffers sized to fit in it. Limited to 50% on VMs with memory less or equal 16GB|
|temp_buffers|string \| integer|false|none|Sets the maximum memory each session uses for temporary table buffers.|
|hash_mem_multiplier|string \| integer|false|none|Multiple of work_mem that hash-based operations may use.|
|enable_parallel_hash|string|false|none|Enables the planner's use of parallel hash plans.|
|maintenance_io_concurrency|string \| integer|false|none|Number of concurrent disk I/O operations used for maintenance work such as vacuum.|
|io_method|string|false|none|Selects the method used to perform asynchronous I/O.|
|io_workers|string \| integer|false|none|Number of I/O worker processes used when io_method is worker.|
|bgwriter_delay|string \| integer|false|none|Sleep time between background writer activity rounds.|
|bgwriter_flush_after|string \| integer|false|none|Amount of data written by the background writer after which the OS is asked to flush it to disk.|
|bgwriter_lru_maxpages|string \| integer|false|none|Maximum number of buffers the background writer writes per round.|
|bgwriter_lru_multiplier|string \| integer|false|none|Multiple of the average recent buffer demand that the background writer cleans per round.|
|statement_timeout|string \| integer|false|none|Abort any statement that runs longer than the specified time. Use 0 to disable.|
|lock_timeout|string \| integer|false|none|Abort any statement that waits longer than the specified time while attempting to acquire a lock. Use 0 to disable.|
|idle_session_timeout|string \| integer|false|none|Terminate any session that has been idle for longer than the specified time. Use 0 to disable.|
|idle_in_transaction_session_timeout|string \| integer|false|none|Terminate any session that has been idle within an open transaction for longer than the specified time. Use 0 to disable.|
|transaction_timeout|string \| integer|false|none|Terminate any statement that takes more than the specified time, even while active. Use 0 to disable.|
|wal_sender_timeout|string \| integer|false|none|Terminate replication connections that are inactive for longer than this time. Use 0 to disable.|
|wal_keep_size|string \| integer|false|none|Minimum size of past WAL files kept in pg_wal for standby servers. Use 0 to disable.|
|min_wal_size|string \| integer|false|none|Minimum size to shrink the WAL to. WAL files are recycled rather than removed when below this size.|
|max_wal_size|string \| integer|false|none|Maximum size WAL can grow between checkpoints. Larger values improve write performance but increase crash recovery time.|
|checkpoint_timeout|string \| integer|false|none|Sets the maximum time between automatic WAL checkpoints.|
|max_slot_wal_keep_size|string \| integer|false|none|Specifies the maximum size of WAL files that replication slots are allowed to retain. Use -1 for unlimited.|
|wal_compression|string|false|none|Compress full-page writes in WAL. Reduces I/O at the cost of CPU. Options vary by PostgreSQL version.|
|wal_buffers|string \| integer|false|none|Sets the number of disk-page buffers in shared memory for WAL. A number without a unit is in 8 kB pages.|
|max_replication_slots|string \| integer|false|none|Maximum number of replication slots. Standbys and logical replication each use slots.|
|max_wal_senders|string \| integer|false|none|Maximum number of simultaneously running WAL sender processes.|
|max_logical_replication_workers|string \| integer|false|none|Maximum number of logical replication workers for subscriptions on this server.|
|max_sync_workers_per_subscription|string \| integer|false|none|Maximum number of table synchronization workers per subscription.|
|logical_decoding_work_mem|string \| integer|false|none|Maximum memory used for logical decoding before changes spill to disk.|
|autovacuum_max_workers|string \| integer|false|none|Maximum number of autovacuum worker processes that can run at the same time. Workers share a single cost-limit budget, so raising this alone may not speed up vacuuming.|
|autovacuum_naptime|string \| integer|false|none|Minimum delay between autovacuum runs. Lower values make autovacuum check for work more frequently.|
|autovacuum_work_mem|string \| integer|false|none|Maximum memory each autovacuum worker uses to track dead tuples. Higher values reduce repeated index-vacuum passes on large tables. Use -1 to fall back to maintenance_work_mem.|
|autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor|string \| number|false|none|Fraction of a table's rows that must change before autovacuum runs. Lower values vacuum large tables more frequently.|
|autovacuum_analyze_scale_factor|string \| number|false|none|Fraction of a table's rows that must change before autovacuum runs ANALYZE to refresh planner statistics.|
|autovacuum_vacuum_insert_scale_factor|string \| number|false|none|Fraction of a table's rows that must be inserted before autovacuum runs. Helps vacuum insert-heavy, rarely-updated tables.|
|autovacuum_vacuum_threshold|string \| integer|false|none|Minimum number of tuple updates or deletes prior to vacuum.|
|autovacuum_analyze_threshold|string \| integer|false|none|Minimum number of tuple inserts, updates, or deletes prior to analyze.|
|autovacuum_vacuum_insert_threshold|string \| integer|false|none|Minimum number of tuple inserts prior to vacuum, or -1 to disable insert vacuums.|
|autovacuum_freeze_max_age|string \| integer|false|none|Age at which to autovacuum a table to prevent transaction ID wraparound.|
|autovacuum_vacuum_cost_limit|string \| integer|false|none|Cost-accounting limit shared across all autovacuum workers before they pause. Use -1 to inherit vacuum_cost_limit.|
|autovacuum_vacuum_cost_delay|string \| integer|false|none|Time autovacuum sleeps when the cost limit is reached. Lower values speed up vacuuming at the cost of more I/O.|
|vacuum_cost_delay|string \| integer|false|none|Time in milliseconds a manual VACUUM sleeps when its cost limit is exceeded. 0 disables cost-based delay.|
|log_min_duration_statement|string \| integer|false|none|Logs statements that run at least this many milliseconds. 0 logs all statements; -1 disables.|
|log_temp_files|string \| integer|false|none|Logs temporary files of at least this size in kilobytes. 0 logs all temporary files; -1 disables.|
|log_lock_waits|string|false|none|Logs a message when a session waits longer than deadlock_timeout to acquire a lock.|

<a id="tocspostgresslowquerypattern"></a>

```json
{
  "queryId": "string",
  "queryText": "string",
  "dbName": "string",
  "dbUser": "string",
  "dbOperation": "string",
  "app": "string",
  "callCount": 0,
  "errorCount": 0,
  "totalDurationUs": 0,
  "avgDurationUs": 0,
  "maxDurationUs": 0,
  "p50DurationUs": 0,
  "p95DurationUs": 0,
  "p99DurationUs": 0,
  "totalRows": 0,
  "totalSharedBlksRead": 0,
  "totalSharedBlksHit": 0,
  "totalCpuTimeUs": 0,
  "totalWalBytes": 0
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|queryId|string|true|none|Stable identifier for the query pattern (normalized SQL).|
|queryText|string|true|none|Normalized query text with literals replaced by placeholders.|
|dbName|string|true|none|Database the query ran in.|
|dbUser|string|true|none|Database user that executed the query.|
|dbOperation|string|true|none|Top-level SQL operation type (for example, SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, UTILITY).|
|app|string|true|none|Value of the Postgres `application_name` for executions matching this pattern.|
|callCount|integer|true|none|Number of times the pattern executed in the window.|
|errorCount|integer|true|none|Number of executions of the pattern that raised an error.|
|totalDurationUs|integer|true|none|Total execution time across all calls, in microseconds.|
|avgDurationUs|integer|true|none|Average execution time per call, in microseconds.|
|maxDurationUs|integer|true|none|Maximum execution time of any call, in microseconds.|
|p50DurationUs|integer|true|none|50th percentile execution time, in microseconds.|
|p95DurationUs|integer|true|none|95th percentile execution time, in microseconds.|
|p99DurationUs|integer|true|none|99th percentile execution time, in microseconds.|
|totalRows|integer|true|none|Total number of rows returned or affected across all calls.|
|totalSharedBlksRead|integer|true|none|Total shared buffer blocks read from disk (cache misses) across all calls.|
|totalSharedBlksHit|integer|true|none|Total shared buffer blocks hit (cache hits) across all calls.|
|totalCpuTimeUs|integer|true|none|Total CPU time across all calls, in microseconds.|
|totalWalBytes|integer|true|none|Total WAL (write-ahead log) bytes generated across all calls.|

|jitEmissionTimeUs|integer|true|none|JIT emission time, in microseconds.|
|jitDeformTimeUs|integer|true|none|JIT deform time, in microseconds.|

Tier of the service: 'development', 'production'. Production services scale, Development are fixed size. Azure services don't support Development tier|
|ipAccessList|[[IpAccessListEntry](#schemaipaccesslistentry)]|true|none|List of IP addresses allowed to access the service|
|minTotalMemoryGb|number|false|none|**Deprecated.** DEPRECATED - inaccurate for services with non-default numbers of replicas. Use `minReplicaMemoryGb` instead. Always absent for horizontal-autoscaling services (replica count is variable).|
|maxTotalMemoryGb|number|false|none|**Deprecated.** DEPRECATED - inaccurate for services with non-default numbers of replicas. Use `maxReplicaMemoryGb` instead. Maximum memory of three workers during auto-scaling in Gb. Available only for 'production' services. Must be a multiple of 12 and lower than or equal to 360 for non paid services or 1068 for paid services. Always absent for horizontal-autoscaling services (replica count is variable).|
|autoscalingMode|string|false|none|Autoscaling mode. "vertical" (the default when omitted) runs a fixed replica count while memory scales between minReplicaMemoryGb and maxReplicaMemoryGb; "horizontal" scales the replica count between minReplicas and maxReplicas at a fixed per-replica memory (minReplicaMemoryGb equal to maxReplicaMemoryGb). Horizontal requires the feature to be enabled for the organization.|
|minReplicaMemoryGb|number|false|none|Minimum total memory of each replica during auto-scaling in Gb. A range in vertical autoscaling; equal to maxReplicaMemoryGb in horizontal (memory is fixed while the replica count scales). Must be a multiple of 4 and greater than or equal to 8.|
|maxReplicaMemoryGb|number|false|none|Maximum total memory of each replica during auto-scaling in Gb. A range in vertical autoscaling; equal to minReplicaMemoryGb in horizontal (memory is fixed while the replica count scales). Must be a multiple of 4 and lower than or equal to 120* for non paid services or 356* for paid services.* - maximum replica size subject to cloud provider hardware availability in your selected region. |
|numReplicas|integer|false|none|Fixed replica count for vertical autoscaling (autoscalingMode "vertical" or omitted). Mutually exclusive with minReplicas/maxReplicas.|
|minReplicas|integer|false|none|Minimum number of replicas. A minReplicas/maxReplicas band scales the replica count in horizontal autoscaling (autoscalingMode "horizontal"). Must be provided together with maxReplicas. Mutually exclusive with numReplicas. Requires horizontal autoscaling to be enabled for the organization, unless autoscalingMode is omitted or "vertical" and minReplicas equals maxReplicas (an equal band is then an accepted vertical fixed count and needs no horizontal entitlement).|
|maxReplicas|integer|false|none|Maximum number of replicas. A minReplicas/maxReplicas band scales the replica count in horizontal autoscaling (autoscalingMode "horizontal"). Must be provided together with minReplicas. Mutually exclusive with numReplicas. Requires horizontal autoscaling to be enabled for the organization, unless autoscalingMode is omitted or "vertical" and minReplicas equals maxReplicas (an equal band is then an accepted vertical fixed count and needs no horizontal entitlement).|
|idleScaling|boolean|false|none|When set to true the service is allowed to scale down to zero when idle. True by default.|
|idleTimeoutMinutes|number|false|none|Set minimum idling timeout (in minutes). Must be >= 5 minutes.|
|isReadonly|boolean|false|none|True if this service is read-only. It can only be read-only if a dataWarehouseId is provided.|
|dataWarehouseId|string|false|none|Data warehouse containing this service|
|backupId|string(uuid)|false|none|Optional backup ID used as an initial state for the new service. When used the region and the tier of the new instance must be the same as the values of the original instance. If the backup is stored in your organization's own bucket, `backupEncryptionConfig` is required; it must be omitted otherwise.|
|backupEncryptionConfig|[BackupEncryptionConfig](#schemabackupencryptionconfig)|false|none|The `encryption_config.json` stored alongside this backup in your bucket, passed through unchanged. Supply the file contents verbatim rather than constructing this object — its shape is versioned and depends on your cloud provider. See [Export backups to your own cloud account](https://clickhouse.com/docs/cloud/manage/backups/export-backups-to-own-cloud-account) for what it contains.<br><br>Accepted only for organizations enrolled in the private preview, and only when the backup is of a service that has transparent data encryption enabled. Such a restore always produces a service with transparent data encryption enabled, inherited from the source service.|
|privateEndpointIds|[string]|false|none|**Deprecated.** DEPRECATED. To associate the service with private endpoints, first create the service, then use the `Update Service Basic Details` endpoint with the `privateEndpointIds` field to modify private endpoints.|
|privatePreviewTermsChecked|boolean|false|none|Accept the private preview terms and conditions. It is only needed when creating the first service in the organization in case of a private preview|
|releaseChannel|string|false|none|Select fast if you want to get new ClickHouse releases as soon as they are available. You'll get new features faster, but with a higher risk of bugs. Select slow if you would like to defer releases to give yourself more time to test. This feature is only available for production services. default is the regular release channel.|
|byocId|string|false|none|This is the ID returned after setting up a region for Bring Your Own Cloud (BYOC). When the byocId parameter is specified, the minReplicaMemoryGb and the maxReplicaGb parameters are required too, with values included among the following sizes: 48, 116, 172, 232.|
|hasTransparentDataEncryption|boolean|false|none|True if the service should have the Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) enabled. TDE is only available for ENTERPRISE organizations tiers and can only be enabled at service creation.|
|endpoints|[[ServiceEndpointChange](#schemaserviceendpointchange)]|false|none|List of service endpoints to enable or disable|
|profile|string|false|none|Custom instance profile. Only available for ENTERPRISE and BYOC organization tiers. Standard values: 'v1-default', 'v1-highmem-xs', 'v1-highmem-s', 'v1-highmem-m', 'v1-highmem-l', 'v1-highmem-xl'. BYOC services may instead use a dynamic BYOC profile configured for their infrastructure (e.g. 'v1-standard-byoc-4'); it requires byocId, and minReplicaMemoryGb and maxReplicaMemoryGb must both equal the profile's memory size. Use the serviceProfiles endpoint to list the profiles available to the organization.|
|complianceType|string|false|none|Type of regulatory compliance for service.|
|tags|[[ResourceTagsV1](#schemaresourcetagsv1)]|false|none|Tags associated with the service.|
|enableCoreDumps|boolean|false|none|Enables the underlying infra for collecting core dumps. Default is enabled.|

|maxReplicaMemoryGb|number|false|none|Maximum auto-scaling memory in Gb for a single replica. Available only for 'production' services. Must be a multiple of 4 and lower than or equal to 120 for non paid services or 356 for paid services. A range in vertical autoscaling; equal to minReplicaMemoryGb in horizontal (memory is fixed while the replica count scales).|
|numReplicas|integer|false|none|Number of replicas for the service. The number of replicas must be between 2 and 50 for the first service in a warehouse. Services that are created in an existing warehouse can have a number of replicas as low as 1. Further restrictions may apply based on your organization's tier and its per-warehouse replica limit. It defaults to 1 for the BASIC tier and 3 for the SCALE and ENTERPRISE tiers. Present only when the service uses vertical autoscaling. For horizontal autoscaling, use minReplicas and maxReplicas instead.|
|minReplicas|integer|false|none|Minimum number of replicas for horizontal autoscaling. Present only when the service uses horizontal autoscaling.|
|maxReplicas|integer|false|none|Maximum number of replicas for horizontal autoscaling. Present only when the service uses horizontal autoscaling.|
|autoscalingMode|string|true|none|Configured autoscaling mode. "vertical" runs a fixed replica count while memory scales between minReplicaMemoryGb and maxReplicaMemoryGb; "horizontal" scales the replica count between minReplicas and maxReplicas at a fixed per-replica memory. This is the baseline configuration; the mode currently applied (which may differ while a schedule entry is active) is currentScaling.effectiveAutoscalingMode.|
|replicaMemoryGb|number|false|none|Fixed memory per replica in Gb for horizontal autoscaling. Present only when the service uses horizontal autoscaling. Must be a multiple of 4, at least 8 Gb, and at most 120 Gb for non paid services or 356 Gb for paid services.|
|idleScaling|boolean|false|none|When set to true the service is allowed to scale down to zero when idle. True by default.|
|idleTimeoutMinutes|number|false|none|Set minimum idling timeout (in minutes). Must be >= 5 minutes.|
|ipAccessList|[[IpAccessListEntry](#schemaipaccesslistentry)]|false|none|List of IP addresses allowed to access the service|
|createdAt|string(date-time)|false|none|Service creation timestamp. ISO-8601.|
|encryptionKey|string|false|none|Optional customer provided disk encryption key|
|encryptionAssumedRoleIdentifier|string|false|none|Optional role to use for disk encryption|
|iamRole|string|false|none|IAM role used for accessing objects in s3|
|privateEndpointIds|[string]|false|none|List of private endpoints|
|availablePrivateEndpointIds|[string]|false|none|List of available private endpoints ids that can be attached to the service|
|dataWarehouseId|string|false|none|Data warehouse containing this service|
|isPrimary|boolean|false|none|True if this service is the primary service in the data warehouse|
|isReadonly|boolean|false|none|True if this service is read-only. It can only be read-only if a dataWarehouseId is provided.|
|releaseChannel|string|false|none|Select fast if you want to get new ClickHouse releases as soon as they are available. You'll get new features faster, but with a higher risk of bugs. Select slow if you would like to defer releases to give yourself more time to test. This feature is only available for production services. default is the regular release channel.|
|byocId|string|false|none|This is the ID returned after setting up a region for Bring Your Own Cloud (BYOC). When the byocId parameter is specified, the minReplicaMemoryGb and the maxReplicaGb parameters are required too, with values included among the following sizes: 48, 116, 172, 232.|
|hasTransparentDataEncryption|boolean|false|none|True if the service should have the Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) enabled. TDE is only available for ENTERPRISE organizations tiers and can only be enabled at service creation.|
|profile|string|false|none|Custom instance profile. Only available for ENTERPRISE and BYOC organization tiers. Standard values: 'v1-default', 'v1-highmem-xs', 'v1-highmem-s', 'v1-highmem-m', 'v1-highmem-l', 'v1-highmem-xl'. BYOC services may instead use a dynamic BYOC profile configured for their infrastructure (e.g. 'v1-standard-byoc-4'); it requires byocId, and minReplicaMemoryGb and maxReplicaMemoryGb must both equal the profile's memory size. Use the serviceProfiles endpoint to list the profiles available to the organization.|
|transparentDataEncryptionKeyId|string|false|none|The ID of the Transparent Data Encryption key used for the service. This is only available if hasTransparentDataEncryption is true.|
|encryptionRoleId|string|false|none|The ID of the IAM role used for encryption. This is only available if hasTransparentDataEncryption is true.|
|complianceType|string|false|none|Type of regulatory compliance for service.|
|tags|[[ResourceTagsV1](#schemaresourcetagsv1)]|false|none|Tags associated with the service.|
|enableCoreDumps|boolean|false|none|True if the service's underline infra is enabled for collecting core dumps. This is an experimental feature|
|scalingSchedule|[ScalingSchedule](#schemascalingschedule)|false|none|none|

<h2 id="tocS_ServiceReplicaScalingPatchRequest">ServiceReplicaScalingPatchRequest</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaservicereplicascalingpatchrequest"></a>
<a id="schema_ServiceReplicaScalingPatchRequest"></a>
<a id="tocSservicereplicascalingpatchrequest"></a>
<a id="tocsservicereplicascalingpatchrequest"></a>

```json
{
  "minReplicaMemoryGb": 16,
  "maxReplicaMemoryGb": 120,
  "autoscalingMode": "vertical",
  "numReplicas": 3,
  "minReplicas": 1,
  "maxReplicas": 5,
  "idleScaling": true,
  "idleTimeoutMinutes": 0
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|minReplicaMemoryGb|number|false|none|Minimum auto-scaling memory in Gb for a single replica. Available only for 'production' services. Must be a multiple of 4 and greater than or equal to 8. A range in vertical autoscaling; equal to maxReplicaMemoryGb in horizontal.|
|maxReplicaMemoryGb|number|false|none|Maximum auto-scaling memory in Gb for a single replica. Available only for 'production' services. Must be a multiple of 4 and lower than or equal to 120 for non paid services or 356 for paid services. A range in vertical autoscaling; equal to minReplicaMemoryGb in horizontal.|
|autoscalingMode|string|false|none|Target autoscaling mode. Omit to keep the service on its current mode. "vertical" runs a fixed replica count while memory scales between minReplicaMemoryGb and maxReplicaMemoryGb; "horizontal" scales the replica count between minReplicas and maxReplicas at a fixed per-replica memory (minReplicaMemoryGb equal to maxReplicaMemoryGb). Switching to horizontal requires the feature to be enabled for the organization.|
|numReplicas|integer|false|none|Fixed replica count for vertical autoscaling (autoscalingMode "vertical"). Mutually exclusive with minReplicas/maxReplicas. When switching to vertical (autoscalingMode "vertical") with numReplicas and no memory, the service's stored baseline per-replica memory is kept as the new vertical range. Please contact support to enable adjustment of numReplicas.|
|minReplicas|integer|false|none|Minimum number of replicas. A minReplicas/maxReplicas band scales the replica count in horizontal autoscaling (autoscalingMode "horizontal"). Must be provided together with maxReplicas. Mutually exclusive with numReplicas. Requires horizontal autoscaling to be enabled for the service, unless autoscalingMode is omitted or "vertical" and minReplicas equals maxReplicas (an equal band is then an accepted vertical fixed count and needs no horizontal entitlement).|
|maxReplicas|integer|false|none|Maximum number of replicas. A minReplicas/maxReplicas band scales the replica count in horizontal autoscaling (autoscalingMode "horizontal"). Must be provided together with minReplicas. Mutually exclusive with numReplicas. Requires horizontal autoscaling to be enabled for the service, unless autoscalingMode is omitted or "vertical" and minReplicas equals maxReplicas (an equal band is then an accepted vertical fixed count and needs no horizontal entitlement).|
|idleScaling|boolean|false|none|When set to true the service is allowed to scale down to zero when idle. True by default.|
|idleTimeoutMinutes|number|false|none|Set minimum idling timeout (in minutes). Must be >= 5 minutes.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|autoscalingMode|vertical|
|autoscalingMode|horizontal|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|regionId|string|true|none|Region in which the BYOC infrastructure will be located|
|accountId|string|true|none|Cloud account ID the BYOC infrastructure is configured for: AWS account ID, GCP project ID, or Azure subscription ID|
|availabilityZoneSuffixes|[string]|false|none|List of availability zone suffixes|
|vpcCidrRange|string|false|none|CIDR range for the ClickHouse-managed VPC. Mutually exclusive with the BYO-VPC fields (`vpcId`, `privateSubnetIds`, `publicSubnetIds`)|
|externalId|string|false|none|AWS only: ExternalID baked into the ClickHouse management role trust policy in your account|
|tenantId|string|false|none|Azure only (required for Azure regions): Entra tenant ID of the subscription|
|servicePrincipalClientId|string|false|none|Azure only (required for Azure regions): client ID of the service principal ClickHouse uses to manage the infrastructure|
|vpcId|string|false|none|BYO-VPC only (AWS and GCP): ID or network name of the customer-provided VPC to deploy into. Requires `privateSubnetIds`|
|privateSubnetIds|[string]|false|none|BYO-VPC only: private subnet IDs or names (1-6 entries on AWS, exactly one on GCP)|
|publicSubnetIds|[string]|false|none|AWS BYO-VPC only: public subnet IDs (at most 6 entries)|
|gcpPodCidrRangeNames|[string]|false|none|GCP BYO-VPC only: secondary IP range names on the subnet to use for pod IPs. Omitted: all secondary ranges are used|
|gcpSharedVpcHostProjectId|string|false|none|GCP BYO-VPC only: Shared VPC host project owning the VPC and subnet, when different from `accountId`|
|tags|[ByocInfrastructureTags](#schemabyocinfrastructuretags)|false|none|none|
|displayName|string|false|none|Human readable name for infrastructure|
